Co-authoring [[achieving-real-business-outcomes-from-artificial-intelligence-and-the-future-of-machine-intelligence]] (O'Reilly Media, 2019), Meley examines production AI case studies across financial fraud detection, autonomous driving telemetry, manufacturing yield optimization, and healthcare (source: BOOKS/AI/2019 Achieving-Real-Business-Outcomes-from-Artificial-Intelligence.pdf, pp. 1–26).

---

chris-miller.name: Chris Miller
chris-miller.eras: 21st-Century Technological Geopolitics, Economic Statecraft & Cold War History
chris-miller.bio:
**Christopher Miller** is Professor of International History at the **Fletcher School of Law and Diplomacy at Tufts University** and Nonresident Senior Fellow at the American Enterprise Institute (AEI), specializing in the history of technology, US–China–Russia geopolitics, and economic statecraft. His international bestseller [[chip-war-the-fight-for-the-worlds-most-critical-technology]] (*Chip War: The Fight for the World's Most Critical Technology*, 2022) won the *Financial Times* Business Book of the Year Award and the Arthur Ross Book Award from the Council on Foreign Relations (source: [[chip-war-the-fight-for-the-worlds-most-critical-technology]], pp. 1–22, 473).

In [[chip-war-the-fight-for-the-worlds-most-critical-technology]], Miller traces the seventy-five-year co-evolution of Silicon Valley, the Pentagon's **Offset Strategies**, East Asian manufacturing ecosystems, **ASML**'s extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography monopoly, and [[morris-chang]]'s **TSMC** pure-play foundry in Taiwan, demonstrating how ultra-concentrated semiconductor chokepoints have become the decisive arena of 21st-century military deterrence and artificial intelligence supremacy.

---

chris-shipley.name: Chris Shipley
chris-shipley.eras: Silicon Valley Technology Foresight, Innovation Ecosystems, and Future-Ready Leadership
chris-shipley.bio:
**Chris Shipley** is a veteran Silicon Valley technology analyst, innovation strategist, and co-leader of the **Silicon Guild**, a consortium of bestselling business and leadership authors (source: [[leading-for-tomorrow]], About the Editors, p. 340). From 1996 to 2009, Shipley served as Executive Producer of the **DEMO Conference**, where she helped launch and spotlight some of the most transformative technologies of the modern internet era—including TiVo, VMware, Salesforce, PalmPilot, and E*Trade—earning recognition from the *San Jose Mercury News* as "the most powerful woman in Silicon Valley you've never heard of."

Co-founder of Guidewire Group and co-author (with Heather McGowan) of *The Adaptation Advantage* (2020) and *The Empathy Advantage* (2023), Shipley specializes in how technological inflection points reshape human work, learning, and identity. In [[leading-for-tomorrow]] (2026), co-edited with [[scott-barry-kaufman]], she curates and synthesizes twenty-six essays from world-renowned thinkers (including [[rita-mcgrath]], [[amy-c-edmondson]], and [[jonathan-haidt]]), charting how leaders can harness generative AI, navigate demographic and geopolitical turbulence, and lead with empathy and strategic foresight.

---

christoph-stuckelberger.name: Christoph Stückelberger
christoph-stuckelberger.eras: 21st-Century Global Ethics, Applied Virtue Ethics & Higher Education Integrity
christoph-stuckelberger.bio:
Prof. Dr. Christoph Stückelberger (born 1951) is a Swiss ethicist, Founder and President of the **Globethics.net Foundation** in Geneva, Professor Emeritus of Ethics at the University of Basel, and visiting professor in Moscow, Enugu (Nigeria), and Beijing.

As lead editor of [[global-ethics-for-leadership-values-and-virtues-for-life]] (2016) with [[walter-fust]] and [[obiora-ike]] and co-editor of [[ethics-in-higher-education-values-driven-leaders-for-the-future]] (2017) with [[divya-singh]], Stückelberger champions a relational ethic that is simultaneously **globally responsible and contextually rooted**.

---

claudia-zeisberger.name: Claudia Zeisberger
claudia-zeisberger.eras: 21st-Century Institutional Private Equity, Venture Capital & Corporate Governance
claudia-zeisberger.bio:
Professor Claudia Zeisberger is Senior Affiliate Professor of Decision Sciences and Entrepreneurship & Family Enterprise at INSEAD and Founder and Academic Director of INSEAD's Global Private Equity Initiative (GPEI). Prior to joining INSEAD in 2005, she spent 16 years in global investment banking across New York, London, Frankfurt, Tokyo, and Singapore.

In [[mastering-private-equity]] (2017, co-authored with [[michael-prahl]] and [[bowen-white]]), Zeisberger synthesizes the full institutional PE/VC lifecycle from fund formation and leveraged buyouts to operational value creation, ESG, and secondaries (source: BOOKS/Private Equity/2017 mastering-private-equity-transformation-via-venture-capital-minority-investments-and-buyouts.pdf, pp. 16, 347).

---

clayton-m-christensen.name: Clayton M. Christensen
clayton-m-christensen.eras: Disruptive Innovation Theory, Jobs-to-Be-Done & Public Sector Transformation
clayton-m-christensen.bio:
Clayton M. Christensen (1952–2020) was the Kim B. Clark Professor of Business Administration at Harvard Business School and co-founder of Innosight and the Clayton Christensen Institute for Disruptive Innovation. Widely regarded as one of the most influential management theorists of the modern era (*The Innovator's Dilemma*, 1997), Christensen extended disruptive innovation and **Jobs-to-Be-Done** theory to healthcare and public education.

In [[disrupting-class-how-disruptive-innovation-will-change-the-way-the-world-learns]] (2008) and his Foreword to [[blended-using-disruptive-innovation-to-improve-schools]] (2015) with [[michael-b-horn]], [[curtis-w-johnson]], and [[heather-staker]], Christensen demonstrated how modular, student-centric online and blended learning will transform K–12 education from a factory-batch system into a mastery-based architecture.

---

clifford-t-bekar.name: Clifford T. Bekar
clifford-t-bekar.eras: Economic History, Institutional Evolution & General Purpose Technologies
clifford-t-bekar.bio:
Clifford T. Bekar is Professor of Economics at Lewis & Clark College, specializing in long-run European and comparative economic history, institutional change, and the historical diffusion of General Purpose Technologies.

In [[economic-transformations-general-purpose-technologies-and-long-term-economic-growth]] (2005), co-authored with [[richard-g-lipsey]] and [[kenneth-i-carlaw]], Bekar reconstructs 10,000 years of GPT revolutions and the institutional conditions explaining why sustained intensive growth emerged in the West.

---

colin-murphy.name: Colin Murphy
colin-murphy.eras: Shared-Use Urban Mobility, Public Transit Integration & Transportation Equity
colin-murphy.bio:
Dr. Colin Murphy is Research and Consulting Director at the Shared-Use Mobility Center (SUMC) in Chicago, specializing in public transit integration, multimodal data standards, and clean urban mobility.

As lead author of *TCRP Research Report 230: Transit and Micromobility* in [[electric-vehicles-light-duty-fuel-economy-and-shared-micromobility]], Murphy analyzes first-and-last-mile bikeshare/e-scooter integration, fare subsidies, and the Mobility Data Specification (MDS).

---

curtis-w-johnson.name: Curtis W. Johnson
curtis-w-johnson.eras: Public Education Reform, Charter Governance & Civic Innovation
curtis-w-johnson.bio:
Curtis W. Johnson (1938–2023) was a senior policy advisor, former Chief of Staff to Minnesota Governor Arne Carlson, Chair of the Twin Cities Metropolitan Council, and co-founder of Education Evolving.

In [[disrupting-class-how-disruptive-innovation-will-change-the-way-the-world-learns]] (2008), co-authored with [[clayton-m-christensen]] and [[michael-b-horn]], Johnson analyzed the political consensus and autonomous charter/team governance structures needed to enable school innovation.

---

daan-j-a-crommelin.name: Daan J. A. Crommelin
daan-j-a-crommelin.eras: 20th/21st-Century Pharmaceutical Biotechnology, Biologics Formulation & Drug Delivery
daan-j-a-crommelin.bio:
Daan J. A. Crommelin, PhD, is Professor Emeritus of Biopharmaceutics at the Utrecht Institute for Pharmaceutical Sciences (Utrecht University, The Netherlands) and a global authority on recombinant protein formulation, liposomes, and pharmaceutical biotechnology.

Co-editing [[pharmaceutical-biotechnology-fundamentals-and-applications]] (4th Ed., 2013) with [[robert-d-sindelar]] and [[bernd-meibohm]], Crommelin anchors the foundational science of biologics formulation and delivery (source: BOOKS/Health Pharma/2013_Book_PharmaceuticalBiotechnology.pdf, pp. 5–9).

---

daniel-kirsch.name: Daniel Kirsch
daniel-kirsch.eras: 21st-Century Enterprise Data Science, Hybrid Cloud & Algorithmic Governance
daniel-kirsch.bio:
Daniel Kirsch is Managing Director at Hurwitz & Associates and an enterprise technology analyst specializing in machine learning governance, hybrid cloud security, and DevOps.

Co-authoring [[machine-learning-for-dummies-ibm-limited-edition]] (2018) with [[judith-hurwitz]], Kirsch maps supervised, unsupervised, reinforcement, and instance-based learning algorithms onto real-world fraud, healthcare, and supply-chain deployments (source: BOOKS/AI/2017 Book ML for Dummies by IBM_.pdf, pp. 2–16, 28–61).

---

daniel-kokotajlo.name: Daniel Kokotajlo
daniel-kokotajlo.eras: 21st-Century AI Forecasting, AGI Governance & Superalignment Research
daniel-kokotajlo.bio:
Daniel Kokotajlo is Executive Director of the AI Futures Project and a former governance researcher at OpenAI (2022–2024), widely recognized for his remarkably accurate 2021 forecast *'What 2026 Looks Like'* and for publicly resigning from OpenAI's non-disparagement equity agreement to warn of AGI safety risks.

In [[ai-2027]] (published April 2025, 71 pp., co-authored with [[scott-alexander]], [[thomas-larsen]], [[eli-lifland]], and [[romeo-dean]]), Kokotajlo leads a month-by-month, quantitatively grounded scenario forecast charting the emergence of recursive AI R&D automation, model weight espionage, misaligned superintelligence (`Agent-1` to `Agent-5`), and the geopolitical race between the U.S. ('OpenBrain') and China ('DeepCent') (source: BOOKS/AI/2025 Book_ai-2027.pdf, pp. 1–36, 46–71).

---

daniel-miller.name: Daniel Miller
daniel-miller.eras: 21st-Century Digital Anthropology, Material Culture & Global Social Media Ethnography
daniel-miller.bio:
Daniel Miller is Professor of Anthropology at University College London (UCL) and a founder of modern material-culture studies and digital anthropology, directing landmark global comparative ethnographies of social networking, smartphones, and everyday digital life.

In [[digital-anthropology]] (2012, co-edited with [[heather-a-horst]]), Miller formulates the six principles of digital anthropology—comparing binary code to money as both universal abstraction and deeply localized cultural particularity (source: BOOKS/Anthropology_/Digital-Anthropology-edited-by-Heather-A.-Horst-and-Daniel-Miller.pdf, pp. 4–17).

---

dave-wright.name: Dave Wright
dave-wright.eras: 21st-Century Enterprise Cloud Architecture, Agentic Workflows & ServiceNow Innovation
dave-wright.bio:
Dave Wright is Chief Innovation Officer at ServiceNow, where he advises global Fortune 500 executives on enterprise workflow architecture, autonomous AI agents, and organizational transformation.

Co-authoring [[infinite-how-visionary-leaders-transform-todays-businesses-into-ai-forward-companies]] (2026) with [[brian-solis]], Wright maps the five-stage evolutionary maturity curve toward the **Infinite Enterprise**, the ROI Paradox of AI valuation, and the emergence of the **Chief Workflow Officer (CWO)** (source: BOOKS/AI/2026 Infinite- Leadership in AI Forward Companies.pdf, pp. 7, 48–75, 148–203).

---

david-baum.name: David Baum
david-baum.eras: 21st-Century Cloud Security Architecture, SIEM Modernization & Data Engineering
david-baum.bio:
David Baum is a technology writer and enterprise architecture analyst who collaborates with O'Reilly Media and cloud data engineering leaders to document modern analytics and cybersecurity operating models.

In [[deploying-a-modern-security-data-lake]] (2022), Baum explains how cloud-native security data lakes, the Connected Applications Model, and Detection-as-Code replace brittle, expensive legacy SIEMs (source: BOOKS/Cloud/Deploying a Modern Security Data Lake.pdf, pp. 1–14, 26–44).

---

david-beyer.name: David Beyer
david-beyer.eras: 21st-Century Venture Capital, Machine Intelligence & Applied Deep Learning
david-beyer.bio:
David Beyer is a Partner at Amplify Partners, focusing on early-stage venture investments in machine intelligence, data infrastructure, and developer tools.

In *The Future of Machine Intelligence: Perspectives from Leading Practitioners* (O'Reilly Media, 2016, 78 pp., synthesized in [[achieving-real-business-outcomes-from-artificial-intelligence-and-the-future-of-machine-intelligence]]), Beyer curates foundational dialogues with Turing Award laureate Yoshua Bengio, Anima Anandkumar, Brendan Frey, Risto Miikkulainen, Benjamin Recht, Daniela Rus, and Zoubin Ghahramani (source: BOOKS/AI/2016 Book OReilly future-of-machine-intelligence.pdf, pp. 1–11, 31, 61).

---

david-cancel.name: David Cancel
david-cancel.eras: 21st-Century Customer-Driven Product Leadership, Conversational Marketing & SaaS
david-cancel.bio:
David Cancel is a five-time serial SaaS entrepreneur—founder of Compete (acquired by WPP), Ghostery, Performable (acquired by HubSpot), and cofounder/CEO of Drift—and former Chief Product Officer at HubSpot, where his product restructuring halved churn and doubled LTV:CAC ahead of HubSpot's IPO.

In [[hypergrowth-how-the-customer-driven-model-is-revolutionizing-business]] (2016), Cancel declares the end of inward-facing Waterfall/Agile cycles in favor of 1:1 customer messaging, Responsible Development, and autonomous three-person engineering teams (source: BOOKS/SaaS/HYPERGROWTH-by-David-Cancel.pdf, pp. 2, 5–16, 22–28).

---

david-gorman.name: David Gorman
david-gorman.eras: Enterprise Distributed Systems & Permissioned Blockchain Engineering
david-gorman.bio:
David Gorman is a Senior Technical Staff Member and Enterprise Blockchain Architect at IBM specializing in Hyperledger Fabric network topology, distributed systems security, and enterprise integration.

In [[getting-started-with-enterprise-blockchain]], Gorman co-authors the architectural blueprints for consortium governance, endorsement policies, and private data collections.

---

david-weisburd.name: David Weisburd
david-weisburd.eras: Experimental Criminology, Crime and Place ('Law of Crime Concentration') & Hot-Spots Policing
david-weisburd.bio:
David Weisburd is Distinguished Professor of Criminology, Law and Society at George Mason University, Walter E. Meyer Professor Emeritus of Law and Criminal Justice at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, and recipient of the Stockholm Prize in Criminology (2010) for pioneering **Place-Randomized Controlled Trials** and formulating the **Law of Crime Concentration at Places**.

In [[handbook-of-quantitative-criminology]] (2010), co-edited with [[alex-r-piquero]], Weisburd synthesizes spatial crime mapping, experimental field trials, and statistical causal inference in criminal justice.

---

dean-cheng.name: Dean Cheng
dean-cheng.eras: Chinese Military Studies, PLA Doctrine, Indo-Pacific Security
dean-cheng.bio:
Dean Cheng is a leading American defense analyst and former Senior Research Fellow for Chinese Political and Military Affairs at the Asian Studies Center of The Heritage Foundation, currently Senior Advisor to the China Program at the U.S. Institute of Peace. Fluent in Mandarin, Cheng has written extensively on Chinese military modernization, aerospace capabilities, information warfare, and Chinese strategic doctrine.

In *Deterrence in the 21st Century*, Cheng authored Chapter 10 ("An Overview of Chinese Thinking About Deterrence"), providing a comprehensive deconstruction of the Chinese concept of *weishe* (coercion/deterrence), explaining how Beijing views deterrence not merely as passive war prevention, but as an active, offensive-defensive instrument to shape adversary behavior and secure strategic objectives without fighting.

---
dean-cheng.recurring_themes:
- [[non-western-strategic-thought]]: The Chinese concept of *weishe* and the Three Warfares (psychological, media, legal).
- [[cross-domain-conflict]]: Space, cyber, and electronic warfare integration in PLA strategy.
- [[deterrence-and-coercion]]: Compellence and coercive diplomacy in cross-strait and Indo-Pacific security.

derric-gilling.name: Derric Gilling
derric-gilling.eras: 21st-Century API Analytics, Usage-Based Monetization & Developer Observability
derric-gilling.bio:
Derric Gilling is cofounder and CEO of Moesif, an API analytics and monetization platform helping API-first engineering and product teams track developer adoption, Time-to-First-Hello, and usage-based billing.

Co-authoring [[api-strategy-for-decision-makers]] (2022) with [[mike-amundsen]], Gilling shows how observability turns invisible API calls into measurable developer-funnel growth and retention metrics (source: BOOKS/Cloud/OReilly-API-Strategy-for-Decision-Makers.pdf, pp. 5–6, 19–43).

---

dinesh-kulkarni.name: Dinesh Kulkarni
dinesh-kulkarni.eras: 21st-Century Cloud Data Sharing, Data Marketplaces & Distributed SaaS
dinesh-kulkarni.bio:
Dinesh Kulkarni is a senior data-platform leader and co-author specializing in secure data sharing, cloud data marketplaces, and enterprise SaaS data monetization.

In [[architecting-data-intensive-saas-applications]] (2021), Kulkarni examines how Sharing by Reference replaces brittle copy-based data exchanges, enabling SaaS ecosystems like Braze on the Snowflake Data Marketplace (source: BOOKS/SaaS/OReilly-Report-Architecting-Data-Intensive-SaaS-Applications.pdf, pp. 3–4, 55–63).

---

divya-singh.name: Divya Singh
divya-singh.eras: Higher Education Governance, Legal Ethics & Distance Learning in Southern Africa
divya-singh.bio:
Advocate Prof. Dr. Divya Singh is a South African legal scholar, Chief Academic Officer at STADIO Higher Education, former Vice Principal of Advisory and Assurance Services at the University of South Africa (UNISA), and Director of Globethics.net Southern Africa.

As lead co-editor of [[ethics-in-higher-education-values-driven-leaders-for-the-future]] (2017) with [[christoph-stuckelberger]], Singh examines university ethical governance, academic integrity in distance e-learning, and preparing graduates for global citizenship.

---

dmitry-adamsky.name: Dmitry Adamsky
dmitry-adamsky.eras: Russian Military Studies, Strategic Culture, Nuclear Strategy
dmitry-adamsky.bio:
Dmitry (Dima) Adamsky is Professor of International Relations and Strategy at the Lauder School of Government, Diplomacy and Strategy at Reichman University (IDC Herzliya), Israel. He has held research appointments at Harvard University's Belfer Center, Columbia University, and the Norwegian Institute for Defence Studies. He is the author of celebrated books such as *The Culture of Military Innovation* (2010) and *Russian Nuclear Orthodoxy* (2019).

Adamsky is one of the world's preeminent experts on Russian strategic thought, military doctrine, and deterrence culture. In *Deterrence in the 21st Century*, Adamsky authored Chapter 9 ("Deterrence à la Ruse: Its Uniqueness, Sources and Implications"), detailing how the Russian concept of *sderzhivanie* blends non-military coercion, information confrontation, strategic deception (*maskirovka*), and holistic nuclear signaling across peacetime and wartime.

---
dmitry-adamsky.recurring_themes:
- [[non-western-strategic-thought]]: Russian *sderzhivanie* versus Western binary deterrence models.
- [[hybrid-threats-and-cyber-warfare]]: Information operations, reflex control, and psychological coercion.
- [[nuclear-strategy-and-strategic-stability]]: Non-strategic nuclear weapons and regional escalation control in Russian doctrine.

doga-dernegi-researchers.name: Doğa Derneği Research Team
doga-dernegi-researchers.eras: 21st-Century Anatolian Conservation Biology, Key Biodiversity Areas & Environmental Policy
doga-dernegi-researchers.bio:
Doğa Derneği (BirdLife Turkey) is Türkiye's premier nature-conservation organization partnering with ecologists, marine researchers (SAD-AFAG), and regional birding societies to inventory and protect Anatolia's Key Biodiversity Areas (*Önemli Doğa Alanları*).

In [[turkiyenin-onemli-doga-alanlari-ege-bolgesi]] (2007, featuring Eray Çağlayan, Cem O. Kıraç, Bahtiyar Kurt, Yalçın Savaş, Ferdi Akarsu, and Rukiye Tanyeri), the team catalogs the Aegean Region's wetlands, coastal habitats, endemic taxa, and conservation pressures (source: BOOKS/Math/03_EGE.pdf, pp. 1–7).

---

dominique-levin.name: Dominique Levin
dominique-levin.eras: 21st-Century SaaS Customer Success, Net Revenue Retention & Post-Sale Growth
dominique-levin.bio:
Dominique Levin is a SaaS executive, Winning by Design partner, and customer-success strategist focused on engineering frictionless post-sale onboarding, recurring customer impact, and compounding Net Revenue Retention.

In [[the-saas-sales-method-for-customer-success-and-account-managers]] (2018, co-authored with [[jacco-van-der-kooij]]), Levin operationalizes Preboarding, Business Orchestration, Customer Health Scores, The Golden Sequence, and Executive Impact Reviews (source: BOOKS/SaaS/Dominique Levin  Jacco van der Kooij  Winning by Design - The SaaS Sales Method for Customer Success  Account Managers_ How to Grow Customers (Sales Blueprints Book 6)-Winning By Design (2018).pdf, pp. 7–16, 48–76).

---

einar-hille.name: Einar Hille
einar-hille.eras: 20th-Century Functional Analysis, Operator Semigroups & Classical Analysis
einar-hille.bio:
Einar Hille (1894–1980) was a towering American mathematician (Yale University, President of the AMS, co-author of the Hille–Yosida theorem in functional analysis) whose analytical rigor shaped 20th-century operator theory and university calculus education.

Honored in [[calculus-one-and-several-variables]] (10th Ed., 2007, with [[saturnino-l-salas]] and [[garret-j-etgen]]), Hille's legacy unites foundational calculus with modern functional analysis (source: BOOKS/Math/C A L C U L U S_ONE AND SEVERAL VARIABLES Artun.pdf, pp. 7–8).

---

eitan-shamir.name: Eitan Shamir
eitan-shamir.eras: Middle Eastern Security, Irregular Warfare, Command Culture
eitan-shamir.bio:
Dr. Eitan Shamir is Director of the Begin-Sadat Center for Strategic Studies (BESA Center) and Associate Professor in the Political Science Department at Bar-Ilan University. A former Senior Officer in the Israeli Ministry of Strategic Affairs, Shamir is the author of *Transforming Command: The Pursuit of Mission Command in the U.S., British, and Israeli Armies*.

In *Deterrence in the 21st Century*, Shamir authored Chapter 14 ("Deterring Violent Non-state Actors"), analyzing cumulative deterrence strategies and Israel's operational doctrine against non-state groups like Hamas and Hezbollah.

---
eitan-shamir.recurring_themes:
- [[violent-non-state-actors]]: Cumulative deterrence and counter-terrorism strategy.
- [[deterrence-and-coercion]]: Tailored deterrence against asymmetric adversaries.

ekrem-akurgal.name: Ekrem Akurgal
ekrem-akurgal.eras: Classical and Anatolian Archaeology, Republican Enlightenment, Greco-Anatolian Synthesis
ekrem-akurgal.bio:
Prof. Dr. Ekrem Akurgal (1911–2002) was Turkey's preeminent classical archaeologist, art historian, and humanist intellectual. Selected during the early Republic as part of Atatürk's educational mobilization to send promising youth to Europe ("You are being sent as sparks; you must return as volcanic fires"), Akurgal studied classical archaeology in Berlin under Gerhart Rodenwaldt between 1932 and 1940.

Returning to Turkey, Akurgal served as a professor at Ankara University's Faculty of Language, History, and Geography (DTCF) for over forty years. He conducted landmark excavations at Bayraklı (Old Smyrna), Phocaea (Foça), Pitane (Çandarlı), Erythrai (Ildırı), and Sinope. Akurgal revolutionized world archaeology by proving that archaic Greek art and philosophy were fundamentally ignited and nurtured by Eastern and Anatolian civilizations (Hittite, Hurrian, Urartian, Phrygian, and Lydian), articulating the concept of the "Anatolian Civilizations Synthesis" (*Anadolu Uygarlıkları Sentezi*).

elena-n-ieno.name: Elena N. Ieno
elena-n-ieno.eras: 21st-Century Marine Biology, Ecological Data Analysis & R Statistical Pedagogy
elena-n-ieno.bio:
Dr. Elena N. Ieno is a marine biologist and senior statistical consultant at Highland Statistics Ltd. (Newburgh, UK).

Co-authoring *A Beginner's Guide to R* (Springer *Use R!*, 2009, 228 pp., synthesized in [[python-and-r-scientific-computing-foundations-for-ai-and-data-science]]) with [[alain-f-zuur]] and [[erik-h-w-g-meesters]], Ieno designs empirical life-science case studies teaching scientists to transition from spreadsheet errors to scripted R workflows (source: BOOKS/AI/2009_Book_ABeginnerSGuideToR.pdf, pp. 4–8).

---

eli-lifland.name: Eli Lifland
eli-lifland.bio:
Eli Lifland is a top-ranked international superforecaster (#1 on the RAND Forecasting Initiative and INFER leaderboards), co-founder of Samotsvety Forecasting, and researcher at the AI Futures Project.

In [[ai-2027]] (2025), Lifland leads the quantitative appendices forecasting compute scaling ($10^{27}$ to $10^{28}$ FLOP), superhuman coding milestones, and algorithmic progress multipliers (source: BOOKS/AI/2025 Book_ai-2027.pdf, pp. 1, 4–6, 51).

---

eli-m-noam.name: Eli M. Noam
eli-m-noam.eras: Media Economics, Telecommunications Policy & Digital Information Management
eli-m-noam.bio:
Eli M. Noam is the Paul Garrett Professor Emeritus of Public Policy and Business Responsibility and Director of the Columbia Institute for Tele-Information (CITI) at Columbia Business School, having also served as a New York State Public Service Commissioner.

In [[media-and-digital-management]] (2019), Noam provides a comprehensive industrial-organization and management framework for content production, near-zero-marginal-cost digital economics, IP law, portfolio risk hedging, and streaming distribution.

---

elias-canetti.name: Elias Canetti
elias-canetti.eras: Interwar Viennese Analytic Modernism & 20th-Century Social Philosophy (1981 Nobel Prize in Literature)
elias-canetti.bio:
Elias Canetti (1905–1994) was a Bulgarian-born Sephardic Jewish novelist, playwright, and social theorist who wrote in German in interwar Vienna before emigrating to London in 1938 after the *Anschluss*. Awarded the 1981 Nobel Prize in Literature, Canetti is celebrated for his modernist novel *Die Blendung* (*Auto-da-Fé*, 1935), his monumental study of mass psychology and totalitarianism *Masse und Macht* (*Crowds and Power*, 1960), and his three-volume autobiography.

As analyzed by [[william-collins-donahue]] in [[the-end-of-modernism-elias-canettis-auto-da-fe]], Canetti's portrayal of sinologist Peter Kien, Therese Krumbholz, and Siegfried Fischerle exposes how ivory-tower humanism and Neo-Kantian inwardness capitulate before fascist crowd fanaticism.

---

erdal-polat.name: Erdal Polat
erdal-polat.eras: Turkish Republican Historiography, History of Science, Cultural Heritage Studies
erdal-polat.bio:
Dr. Erdal Polat is a contemporary Turkish historian, academic, and researcher focusing on the cultural, intellectual, and institutional history of the early Turkish Republic. His scholarship investigates the scientific and institutional foundations established during Mustafa Kemal Atatürk’s nation-building process, particularly the role of archaeology, anthropology, and language studies in shaping modern civic identity.

In his comprehensive study published in the *Atatürk Araştırma Merkezi Dergisi* (2024), Polat analyzes the systematic archaeological policies implemented between 1923 and the 1950s, detailing how Atatürk transformed archaeology from an imperial treasure-hunting activity into a rigorous state discipline aimed at proving Anatolia's universal role as a cradle of civilization. Polat examines the life and legacy of Prof. Dr. Ekrem Akurgal, who was sent abroad to Germany by state scholarship in the 1930s and returned to establish the modern school of classical and Anatolian archaeology.

eric-r-kandel.name: Eric R. Kandel
eric-r-kandel.eras: Molecular Neurobiology of Memory, Neuroaesthetics & Bridging the Two Cultures (2000 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine)
eric-r-kandel.bio:
Eric R. Kandel (born 1929 in Vienna) is University Professor Emeritus of Biochemistry and Biophysics at Columbia University, Senior Investigator at the Howard Hughes Medical Institute, and recipient of the **2000 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine** for discovering the molecular and synaptic mechanisms of short- and long-term memory storage in neurons (using the marine snail *Aplysia*).

In [[reductionism-in-art-and-brain-science-bridging-the-two-cultures]] (2016), Kandel bridges C. P. Snow's 'Two Cultures' by showing how post-WWII New York School Abstract Expressionists (de Kooning, Pollock, Rothko, Louis, Flavin, Turrell) used artistic reductionism of form, line, color, and light in parallel with neurobiological reductionism—shifting visual perception from bottom-up figurative recognition to top-down creative imagination (the **Beholder's Share**).

---

eric-w-robinson.name: Eric W. Robinson
eric-w-robinson.eras: Contemporary Classical Greek Constitutional & Political Historiography
eric-w-robinson.bio:
**Eric W. Robinson** is Professor of History at Indiana University Bloomington and a leading classical historian specializing in ancient Greek democracy and political institutions. In his landmark monograph [[the-first-democracies-early-popular-government-outside-athens]] (*The First Democracies: Early Popular Government Outside Athens*, *Historia Einzelschriften* 101, Stuttgart: Franz Steiner Verlag, 1997; followed by *Democracy Beyond Athens: Popular Government in the Greek Classical Age*, 2011), Robinson dismantled the Athenocentric orthodoxy that *demokratia* was invented solely in Athens under Solon or Cleisthenes (source: [[the-first-democracies-early-popular-government-outside-athens]], pp. 1–3 [pp. 153–155]).

By combining Aristotle's *Politics*, Herodotus, Aeschylus, and archaic epigraphy across seventeen Greek city-states and colonies—including **Achaea, Acragas, Ambracia, Argos, Chios, Cyrene, Heraclea Pontica, Mantineia, Megara, Naxos, Samos, and Syracuse**—Robinson proved that popular governments (*demokratiai*) emerged independently across the archaic Greek world, Ionian Anatolia, and Magna Graecia by the mid-sixth century BC, well before 480 BC and independent of Athenian constitutional influence.

---

erik-h-w-g-meesters.name: Erik H.W.G. Meesters
erik-h-w-g-meesters.eras: 21st-Century Marine Ecosystem Modeling & R Statistical Programming
erik-h-w-g-meesters.bio:
Dr. Erik H.W.G. Meesters is a senior researcher in coral reef ecology and marine biometrics at Wageningen Marine Research / IMARES (Texel, The Netherlands).

In *A Beginner's Guide to R* (Springer *Use R!*, 2009, 228 pp., synthesized in [[python-and-r-scientific-computing-foundations-for-ai-and-data-science]]), Meesters co-develops the R programming, plotting, and statistical scripting curriculum for environmental and biological researchers (source: BOOKS/AI/2009_Book_ABeginnerSGuideToR.pdf, pp. 4–8).

---

ethan-mollick.name: Ethan Mollick
ethan-mollick.eras: 21st-Century Generative AI Collaboration, Wharton Innovation & Disruptive Pedagogy
ethan-mollick.bio:
Ethan Mollick (PhD, MIT Sloan School of Management) is Associate Professor of Management at the Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania and Co-Director of Wharton Generative AI Labs, where he leads empirical field experiments with Boston Consulting Group (BCG) on human–AI collaboration.

In his *New York Times* bestseller [[co-intelligence-living-and-working-with-ai]] (2024, 114 pp. analytical summary edition), Mollick formulates the **Four Rules for Co-Intelligence**, the **Jagged Technological Frontier**, **Centaurs vs. Cyborgs** workflow architectures, and the transformation of AI into Person, Creative, Coworker, Tutor (solving Bloom's Two-Sigma Problem), and Coach (source: BOOKS/AI/2024 Co-Intelligence PDF Summary_.pdf, pp. 3–11, 31, 61, 91).

---

fernando-pizarro.name: Fernando Pizarro
fernando-pizarro.eras: 21st-Century SaaS Sales Operations, Revenue Blueprints & B2B Growth
fernando-pizarro.bio:
Fernando Pizarro is a SaaS revenue strategist, technology author, and Winning by Design partner who co-authored and edited the foundational *Sales Blueprints* series for scaling recurring-revenue teams.

In [[blueprints-for-a-saas-sales-organization]] (2018, with [[jacco-van-der-kooij]]) and as editor of [[the-saas-sales-method-for-customer-success-and-account-managers]] (2018), Pizarro translates post-Series A SaaS scaling into repeatable pods, content fuel, and data-driven Sales Operations Centers (source: BOOKS/SaaS/(Winning By Design) Jacco Van Der Kooij and Fernando Pizarro - Blueprints for a SaaS Sales Organization-Fernando Pizzaro, Jacco Van Der Kooij (2017) (2).pdf, pp. 4–7).

---

flexera-research.name: Flexera Research
flexera-research.eras: 21st-Century Enterprise IT Asset Management, FinOps & Cloud Spend Governance
flexera-research.bio:
Flexera Research is the empirical benchmarking arm of Flexera, publishing annual global surveys on enterprise cloud adoption, IT Asset Management (ITAM), Software Asset Management (SAM), and FinOps.

In [[state-of-it-asset-management-2022]] (2022, surveying 465 enterprise IT leaders), Flexera documents the acute governance gap between legacy vendor-audit compliance (consuming 83% of SAM time) and the rapidly expanding SaaS, public-cloud, and container estate (source: BOOKS/Cloud/itam-report-state-of-it-asset-management-2022.pdf, pp. 6–9, 33–42).

---

francesc-miralles.name: Francesc Miralles
francesc-miralles.eras: 21st-Century Personal Development, Existential Psychology & Literary Journalism
francesc-miralles.bio:
Francesc Miralles (born 1968 in Barcelona) is a Spanish journalist, novelist, and bestselling author specializing in psychology, spirituality, and purposeful living.

In [[ikigai-the-japanese-secret-to-a-long-and-happy-life]] (2016/2017, with [[hector-garcia]]), Miralles weaves Viktor Frankl's Logotherapy, Csikszentmihalyi's Flow, Stoicism, and Japanese *wabi-sabi* into a holistic longevity framework (source: BOOKS/Health Pharma/Ikigai _ the Japanese secret to a long and happy life ( PDFDrive ).pdf, pp. 3, 8–108).

---

francesco-giumelli.name: Francesco Giumelli
francesco-giumelli.eras: International Sanctions, Coercive Diplomacy, European Foreign Policy
francesco-giumelli.bio:
Dr. Francesco Giumelli is Associate Professor of International Relations at the University of Groningen. He is an internationally recognized scholar on economic sanctions, illicit trade, and EU foreign policy, having authored books such as *Coercing, Constraining and Signalling: Explaining UN and EU Sanctions After the Cold War*.

In *Deterrence in the 21st Century*, Giumelli authored Chapter 18 ("Targeted Sanctions and Deterrence in the Twenty-first Century"), analyzing the mechanics of smart sanctions within cross-domain deterrence frameworks.

---
francesco-giumelli.recurring_themes:
- [[cross-domain-conflict]]: Economic sanctions and financial leverage as non-kinetic coercive instruments.
- [[deterrence-and-coercion]]: Signaling and constraining functions of targeted sanctions.

frans-johansson.name: Frans Johansson
frans-johansson.eras: 21st-Century Intersectional Innovation, Diversity-Driven Creativity & Strategic Entrepreneurship
frans-johansson.bio:
Frans Johansson (born 1968) is a Swedish-American writer, entrepreneur, and CEO of The Medici Group (educated at Brown University and Harvard Business School) who pioneered the study of cross-disciplinary innovation.

In [[the-medici-effect-what-elephants-and-epidemics-can-teach-us-about-innovation]] (2004/2006), Johansson coined the **Medici Effect** to explain how stepping into the **Intersection** of diverse disciplines, cultures, and domains (such as Renaissance Florence or Mick Pearce's termite-mound biomimetic architecture) ignites exponential creative breakthroughs.

---

frans-osinga.name: Frans Osinga
frans-osinga.eras: Contemporary [[strategic-studies]], Military Theory, Modern Air Power & Operational Art
frans-osinga.bio:
Air Commodore Prof. Dr. Frans Osinga is Professor of Military Operational Art and Sciences and Chair of the War Studies Department at the Faculty of Military Sciences, Netherlands Defence Academy (NLDA), as well as Special Professor in War Studies at Leiden University. A former Royal Netherlands Air Force F-16 pilot and graduate of the Netherlands Defence College, Osinga earned his Ph.D. at Leiden University in 2005 with his seminal work *Science, Strategy and War: The Strategic Theory of John Boyd*.

Osinga is one of Europe's leading military theorists, specializing in command and control, operational art, strategic culture, air power theory, and contemporary deterrence. In *Deterrence in the 21st Century*, co-edited with Tim Sweijs, Osinga investigates the conceptual and operational adaptations required by Western defense establishments facing renewed great power competition, hybrid threats, and emerging disruptive military technologies.

---
frans-osinga.recurring_themes:
- [[deterrence-and-coercion]]: Reassessment of deterrence in European and transatlantic defense architecture.
- [[cross-domain-conflict]]: Synergy between conventional, nuclear, cyber, and non-kinetic power projection.
- [[rationality-and-decision-making]]: Integrating operational decision loops, Boyd's OODA loop, and psychological variables into strategic theory.
- [[hybrid-threats-and-cyber-warfare]]: Countering sub-threshold aggression and grey-zone operations.

fredric-jameson.name: Fredric Jameson
fredric-jameson.eras: Western Marxism, Critical Theory & Postmodern Cultural Studies
fredric-jameson.bio:
Fredric Jameson (1934–2024) was an American literary critic, philosopher, and Knut Schmidt-Nielsen Professor of Comparative Literature at Duke University, universally recognized as the foremost anglophone Marxist cultural theorist of the late 20th and early 21st centuries (*The Political Unconscious*, *Postmodernism, or, The Cultural Logic of Late Capitalism*).

In his substantive Foreword to [[jacques-attali]]'s [[noise-the-political-economy-of-music]], Jameson situates Attali's political economy of sound beyond Althusserian structuralism and Max Weber's sociology of musical rationalization, highlighting music's anticipatory capacity to register emergent social realities.

---

garret-j-etgen.name: Garret J. Etgen
garret-j-etgen.bio:
Garret J. Etgen is Professor of Mathematics at the University of Houston specializing in ordinary differential equations and modernizing undergraduate calculus pedagogy.

Co-authoring [[calculus-one-and-several-variables]] (10th Ed., 2007), Etgen integrated 1,200+ visual illustrations, interdisciplinary applied projects, and Skill Mastery Review sets across 1,171 pages (source: BOOKS/Math/C A L C U L U S_ONE AND SEVERAL VARIABLES Artun.pdf, pp. 7–12).

---

gary-marchant.name: Gary Marchant
gary-marchant.eras: Science & Technology Law, Regulatory Governance & National Academies Energy Policy
gary-marchant.bio:
Gary E. Marchant is Regents' Professor of Law and Director of the Center for Law, Science and Innovation at Arizona State University, and Chair of the National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine (NASEM) Committee on Assessment of Technologies for Improving Fuel Economy of Light-Duty Vehicles (Phase 3).

In [[electric-vehicles-light-duty-fuel-economy-and-shared-micromobility]], Marchant chairs the 457-page NASEM consensus study mapping the 2025–2035 transition from advanced internal combustion engines and hybrids to zero-emission battery electric and fuel-cell vehicles.

---

gilit-saporta.name: Gilit Saporta
gilit-saporta.eras: 21st-Century Fintech Fraud Intelligence, AML Analytics & Adversarial Data Science
gilit-saporta.bio:
Gilit Saporta is Director of Fraud Analytics at DoubleVerify with over two decades of hands-on leadership in online fraud prevention, risk analytics, and financial-crime intelligence at PayPal, Forter, and leading fintech organizations.

In [[practical-fraud-prevention]] (2022, co-authored with [[shoshana-maraney]]), Saporta codifies adversarial fraudster archetypes, dynamic risk-vs.-friction calibration, story-based ML modeling, and SQL/Python defense frameworks across eCommerce, consumer banking, marketplaces, and AML (source: BOOKS/Cloud/3683-practical-fraud-prevention.pdf, pp. 2, 19–133).

---

gjorgji-georgievski.name: Gjorgji Georgievski
gjorgji-georgievski.eras: 21st-Century Cloud Data Pipelines, Streaming Ingestion & SaaS Architecture
gjorgji-georgievski.bio:
Gjorgji Georgievski is a cloud data systems architect specializing in high-volume ELT pipelines, schema evolution, and streaming-vs.-batch ingestion architectures on Snowflake.

Co-authoring [[architecting-data-intensive-saas-applications]] (2021), Georgievski outlines best practices for processing raw and conformed datasets at scale inside customer-facing applications (source: BOOKS/SaaS/OReilly-Report-Architecting-Data-Intensive-SaaS-Applications.pdf, pp. 3–4, 43–53).

---

glenn-kreisberg.name: Glenn Kreisberg
glenn-kreisberg.eras: North American Archaeoastronomy, Megalithic Research, Radio Archaeology
glenn-kreisberg.bio:
Glenn Kreisberg is a radio frequency engineer, researcher, and author based in Woodstock, New York. He is the former vice president of the New England Antiquities Research Association (NEARA) and the founder of the Empire State Antiquities Research Association. Kreisberg specializes in the archaeoastronomy, electromagnetic properties, and spatial orientations of prehistoric stone structures and petroforms across the Northeastern United States.

As editor of *Lost Knowledge of the Ancients* (2010) and *Mysteries of the Ancient Past* (Bear & Company), Kreisberg assembled leading alternative historians, geologists, and archaeoastronomers to challenge conventional dogmas regarding ancient technologies, acoustics, and celestial tracking systems.

graham-hancock.name: Graham Hancock
graham-hancock.eras: Contemporary Alternative Archaeology, Catastrophism, Revisionist Prehistory, Investigative Non-Fiction
graham-hancock.bio:
Graham Hancock (born 2 August 1950 in Edinburgh, Scotland) is a British author, journalist, and independent researcher recognized globally for his investigations into human prehistory, antediluvian civilizations, and ancient mysteries. Formerly the East Africa correspondent for *The Economist* and a writer for *The Sunday Times* and *The Guardian*, Hancock turned his investigative journalism background toward archaeology and mythology in the early 1990s, beginning with *The Sign and the Seal* (1992).

Hancock's work contends that a sophisticated, technologically or spiritually advanced civilization existed during the late Pleistocene epoch and was largely eradicated by catastrophic global upheavals between 12,800 and 11,600 years ago (the Younger Dryas period). He posits that survivors of this lost civilization transmitted fragments of high science, astronomical knowledge, and architectural engineering to hunter-gatherer populations worldwide—giving rise to megalithic structures such as the Giza Pyramids, Göbekli Tepe, Tiwanaku, and ancient Amazonian earthworks. While frequently contested by mainstream academic consensus, Hancock's work has fostered international public interest in archaeoastronomy, paleoclimatology, and the Younger Dryas Impact Hypothesis.

harry-kalven-jr.name: Harry Kalven, Jr.
harry-kalven-jr.eras: Mid-20th Century American Legal Realism & Civil Liberties
harry-kalven-jr.bio:
Harry Kalven, Jr. (1912–1990) was a preeminent American legal scholar, professor at the University of Chicago Law School, and a leading voice in civil liberties and constitutional law. As the chairman of the committee appointed by President George W. Beadle in 1967, Kalven led the drafting of this seminal report which sought to define the institutional boundaries of academic freedom versus political activism (source: ARTICLES-REPORTS/Democracy/KalvenReport.pdf, p. 1). His work is deeply connected to the broader discourse on institutional integrity and the limits of state power, resonating with themes found in [[deterrence-in-the-21st-century]] regarding the stability of institutions under pressure, and [[the-evolution-of-cooperation]] regarding the rules that govern collective action within diverse communities. Kalven’s insistence on the university as a 'community of scholars' rather than a 'lobby' reflects a sophisticated understanding of organizational identity and the preservation of intellectual capital against political fashions (source: ARTICLES-REPORTS/Democracy/KalvenReport.pdf, p. 1).

---

heather-a-horst.name: Heather A. Horst
heather-a-horst.eras: 21st-Century Digital Anthropology, Media Ethnography & Material Culture
heather-a-horst.bio:
Heather A. Horst is a leading digital anthropologist and Director of the Institute for Culture and Society (Western Sydney University; formerly RMIT and UC Irvine) whose ethnographic research examines mobile phones, everyday digital media, and financial technologies across the Caribbean, Pacific, and global cities.

Co-editing [[digital-anthropology]] (2012) with [[daniel-miller]], Horst co-authored the discipline's foundational six-principle prospectus challenging romanticized myths of pre-digital authenticity (source: BOOKS/Anthropology_/Digital-Anthropology-edited-by-Heather-A.-Horst-and-Daniel-Miller.pdf, pp. 4–17).

---

heather-staker.name: Heather Staker
heather-staker.eras: Blended Learning Taxonomy & Student-Centered School Design
heather-staker.bio:
Heather Staker (MBA, Harvard Business School) is President of Ready to Blend and former Senior Research Fellow for Education at the Clayton Christensen Institute, where she conducted the empirical fieldwork mapping K–12 blended schools across North America.

In [[blended-using-disruptive-innovation-to-improve-schools]] (2015), co-authored with [[michael-b-horn]], Staker defines the sustaining vs. disruptive models of blended learning and provides the 7-step school design blueprint.

---

hector-garcia.name: Héctor García
hector-garcia.eras: 21st-Century Japanese Culture, Longevity Journalism & Applied Philosophy
hector-garcia.bio:
Héctor García (born 1981 in Spain; known as Kirai) is a former CERN software engineer and longtime Tokyo resident whose essays and books interpret Japanese culture, craftsmanship, and longevity for global audiences.

Co-authoring [[ikigai-the-japanese-secret-to-a-long-and-happy-life]] (2016/2017) with [[francesc-miralles]], García conducted field interviews in Ogimi, Okinawa to distill the lifestyle, diet, and existential purpose of the world's longest-lived communities (source: BOOKS/Health Pharma/Ikigai _ the Japanese secret to a long and happy life ( PDFDrive ).pdf, pp. 3, 8–16).

---

helio-fred-garcia.name: Helio Fred Garcia
helio-fred-garcia.eras: Contemporary Crisis Management, Executive Rhetoric, and Strategic Communication
helio-fred-garcia.bio:
**Helio Fred Garcia** is President of the Logos Consulting Group and Executive Director of the Logos Institute for Crisis Management and Executive Leadership (source: [[influencing-leaders]], About the Authors, pp. 230–231). For more than four decades, Garcia has advised CEOs, heads of state, and senior military commanders on high-stakes crisis response, investor relations, and strategic persuasion.

Academically trained in philosophy and classical rhetoric at New York University and Columbia University, Garcia serves as an adjunct professor of management at **NYU Stern School of Business** and an adjunct professor of strategic communication at **Columbia University**. He is also a longtime guest lecturer and leadership instructor for the **United States Marine Corps Command and Staff College** and the **U.S. Army War College**. Author of *The Power of Communication*, *The Agony of Decision*, and *Words on Fire*, Garcia brings a rigorous philosophical and behavioral framework to executive counsel. In [[influencing-leaders]] (2026), co-authored with [[james-e-lukaszewski]], he translates the art of executive influence into teachable mental models—demonstrating how trusted advisors diagnose unstated leadership anxieties, distill complex options onto a single page, and protect institutional integrity under pressure.

---

henry-p-stapp.name: Henry P. Stapp
henry-p-stapp.eras: 20th/21st-Century Quantum Foundations, S-Matrix Theory & Quantum Mind-Brain Physics
henry-p-stapp.bio:
Henry P. Stapp is a senior theoretical physicist at the University of California's Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory who worked with Wolfgang Pauli and Werner Heisenberg and pioneered research on Bell nonlocality, S-matrix theory, and the role of conscious observation in von Neumann quantum mechanics.

In [[mind-matter-and-quantum-mechanics]] (3rd Ed., 2009), Stapp formulates the Heisenberg/James model linking intentional human attention, Process 1 collapse, and the Quantum Zeno Effect to neuroplasticity (source: BOOKS/Physics/Henry Stapp - Mind Matter and Quantum mechanics.pdf, pp. 5, 7–11).

---

hugh-everett-iii.name: Hugh Everett III
hugh-everett-iii.eras: 20th-Century Quantum Foundations, Many-Worlds Interpretation & Operations Research
hugh-everett-iii.bio:
Hugh Everett III (1930–1982) was an American physicist and mathematician who completed his PhD at Princeton University's Palmer Physical Laboratory under John A. Wheeler before pioneering operations research, game-theoretic defense analysis, and generalized Lagrange multipliers at the Pentagon's Weapons Systems Evaluation Group.

In his legendary 1957 Princeton thesis [[on-the-foundations-of-quantum-mechanics-relative-state-formulation]], Everett eliminated external wavefunction collapse in favor of pure universal unitary evolution and 'relative states'—birthing the Many-Worlds Interpretation of quantum mechanics (source: BOOKS/Physics/Everett short thesis as defended.pdf, pp. 1–2).

---

hulya-apaydin.name: Hülya Apaydın
hulya-apaydin.eras: 21st-Century Clinical Neurology, Movement Disorders & Patient Education (Türkiye)
hulya-apaydin.bio:
Prof. Dr. Hülya Apaydın is a senior neurologist in the Parkinson's Disease and Movement Disorders Unit, Department of Neurology, Istanbul University Cerrahpaşa Faculty of Medicine.

Co-authoring [[parkinson-hastaligi-hasta-ve-yakinlari-icin-el-kitabi]] (5th Ed., 2013), she provides accessible clinical guidance on Parkinson's diagnosis, Levodopa/COMT/MAO-B pharmacotherapy, and holistic care for Turkish patients and families (source: BOOKS/Health Pharma/Parkinson-Hastaligi-Hasta-ve-Yakinlari-icin-El-Kitabi.pdf, pp. 1–5, 10).

---

iain-staffell.name: Iain Staffell
iain-staffell.eras: Sustainable Energy Systems, Power Grid Decarbonization & Techno-Economic Modeling
iain-staffell.bio:
Iain Staffell is Professor of Sustainable Energy Systems at the Centre for Environmental Policy, Imperial College London, and co-creator of the *Renewables.ninja* and *Electric Insights* platforms advising governments and the IPCC on renewable power integration.

In [[monetizing-energy-storage-a-toolkit-to-assess-future-cost-and-value]] (2023), co-authored with [[oliver-schmidt]], Staffell models the system-level economics, learning rates, and arbitrage revenues of twelve grid storage technologies.

---

ibrahim-gosterir.name: İbrahim Gösterir
ibrahim-gosterir.eras: Contemporary Turkish Folklore, Folk Literature Scholarship, Cultural Anthropology
ibrahim-gosterir.bio:
İbrahim Gösterir (born 1965 in Çorum) is a Turkish educator, folklorist, writer, and poet (writing under the pen name *Ozanî*). He graduated from Ankara University's Faculty of Language, History, and Geography (DTCF) in 1986 and has served as a history teacher and cultural researcher across Turkey (source: BOOKS/Art/73010,cilt1pdf.pdf, p. 33).

Gösterir has dedicated his scholarly career to documenting, archiving, and analyzing the oral traditions, dialects, and folk literature of the Çorum and Central Anatolian regions. His published works include the comprehensive *Çorum Yöresi Ağızları Sözlüğü* (Dictionary of Çorum Regional Dialects, 500 pp., 4th ed. 2020), *Ölüm Var Ayrılık Var - Çorum Manileri* (360 pp., 2011), *Bahar Türküleri* (2014), *Çorum Halk Kültüründe Gülmece* (Humor in Çorum Folk Culture, 320 pp., 2016), as well as monographic studies on regional minstrels *Âşık Haydar Kılıç (Ozan Garip)* (2017) and *Alıcıklı Âşık Hicabî* (2017).

As editor and compiler of *Âşık Borani: Söz İnsanın Aynasıdır* (2020), Gösterir performed a comprehensive decade-long critical compilation of Borani's printed books, archival manuscripts, newspaper columns, and oral performances into a definitive two-volume academic edition (source: BOOKS/Art/73010,cilt1pdf.pdf, pp. 31–36).

---
ibrahim-gosterir.recurring_themes:
- [[asik-and-minstrel-tradition]]: Archiving oral folk poetry and preserving minstrel heritage.
- [[turkish-folk-literature]]: Lexicographical and literary analysis of Anatolian folk verse forms.
- [[universal-love-and-human-dignity]]: Documenting the humanist philosophy of Central Anatolian bardic culture.

igor-yevgenyevich-irodov.name: Igor Yevgenyevich Irodov
igor-yevgenyevich-irodov.bio:
Igor Yevgenyevich Irodov (1923–2002) was a Soviet physicist, World War II veteran, and longtime professor of general physics at the Moscow Engineering Physics Institute (MEPhI), globally renowned for authoring benchmark university physics problem collections.

His classic [[problems-in-general-physics]] (Mir Publishers, 1981) remains the gold standard for Physics Olympiad and honors university training across mechanics, thermodynamics, electrodynamics, optics, and atomic/nuclear physics (source: BOOKS/Physics/1981 Irodov-Problems_in_General_Physics.pdf, pp. 10–11, 51).

---

irakli-nadareishvili.name: Irakli Nadareishvili
irakli-nadareishvili.bio:
Irakli Nadareishvili is an enterprise software architect, technology executive, and adjunct faculty contributor at Temple University whose work focuses on microservices architecture, Event Sourcing, CQRS, and cloud-native engineering organizations.

Co-authoring [[microservices-up-and-running]] (2021) with [[ronnie-mitra]], Nadareishvili details how bounded-context data ownership, Terraform IaC pipelines, and Argo CD GitOps reduce inter-team coordination costs (source: BOOKS/Cloud/Microservices-Up-and-Running_complete.pdf, pp. 4–5, 91–194).

---

isabelle-duyvesteyn.name: Isabelle Duyvesteyn
isabelle-duyvesteyn.eras: Modern History of War, Strategic Culture, Terrorism & Insurgency
isabelle-duyvesteyn.bio:
Prof. Dr. Isabelle Duyvesteyn is Professor of International Studies and Global History at the Institute of History, Leiden University. An elected member of the Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences (KNAW), Duyvesteyn is an internationally prominent scholar of the history of war, strategic culture, emotions in international conflict, and non-state violence.

In *Deterrence in the 21st Century*, Duyvesteyn (with Samuel Zilincik) authored Chapter 24 ("Deterrence: A Continuation of Emotional Life with the Admixture of Violent Means"), examining how fear, anger, pride, and humiliation shape state behavior in military crises.

---
isabelle-duyvesteyn.recurring_themes:
- [[rationality-and-decision-making]]: Emotional and cultural dynamics in crisis bargaining.
- [[strategic-studies]]: Historical analysis of strategic decision-making and war termination.

ismail-zileli.name: İsmail Zileli
ismail-zileli.bio:
Specialist Physiotherapist İsmail Zileli specializes in movement rehabilitation and caregiver-assisted exercise design for chronic neurological conditions.

Co-authoring [[parkinson-hastaligi-hasta-ve-yakinlari-icin-el-kitabi]] (2013), he contributed practical home-exercise routines supporting mobility and quality of life in Parkinson's care (source: BOOKS/Health Pharma/Parkinson-Hastaligi-Hasta-ve-Yakinlari-icin-El-Kitabi.pdf, pp. 1, 6).

---

j-michael-spector.name: J. Michael Spector
j-michael-spector.eras: Instructional Systems Design, Complex Learning Assessment & Educational Technology
j-michael-spector.bio:
J. Michael Spector is Professor of Learning Technologies at the University of North Texas, former President of the Association for Educational Communications and Technology (AECT), and Editor of the *Handbook of Research on Educational Communications and Technology*.

In [[educational-technology-a-primer-for-the-21st-century]] (2019), Spector synthesizes cognitive learning science, ADDIE instructional design, and Design-Based Research (DBR).

---

jaap-hage.name: Jaap Hage
jaap-hage.eras: Philosophy of Law, Legal Logic, Artificial Intelligence & Comparative Jurisprudence
jaap-hage.bio:
Jaap Hage is Professor of Foundations and Methods of Law at Maastricht University Faculty of Law (The Netherlands), internationally recognized for his work on legal logic (*Reasoning with Rules*), defeasible legal reasoning, deontic ontology, and comparative jurisprudence.

As lead editor and author of Chapters 1, 2, 3, and 15 of [[introduction-to-law]] (2017) alongside [[antonia-waltermann]] and [[bram-akkermans]], Hage formulates the universal building blocks of positive law, legal certainty, duties/competences, and the Hart–Dworkin debate.

---

jacco-van-der-kooij.name: Jacco van der Kooij
jacco-van-der-kooij.eras: 21st-Century Revenue Architecture, Recurring-Revenue Science & SaaS Sales
jacco-van-der-kooij.bio:
Jacco van der Kooij is the founder of Winning by Design (San Francisco), a global revenue-architecture advisory firm that pioneered scientific, bowtie-based recurring-revenue operating models and the SPICED diagnostic framework for B2B SaaS companies.

Across [[blueprints-for-a-saas-sales-organization]] (2018, with [[fernando-pizarro]]) and [[the-saas-sales-method-for-customer-success-and-account-managers]] (2018, with [[dominique-levin]]), van der Kooij codifies buyer-centric pods, Impact-over-Needs diagnosis, and Net Revenue Retention above 130% (source: BOOKS/SaaS/(Winning By Design) Jacco Van Der Kooij and Fernando Pizarro - Blueprints for a SaaS Sales Organization-Fernando Pizzaro, Jacco Van Der Kooij (2017) (2).pdf, pp. 6–9, 32; BOOKS/SaaS/Dominique Levin  Jacco van der Kooij  Winning by Design - The SaaS Sales Method for Customer Success  Account Managers_ How to Grow Customers (Sales Blueprints Book 6)-Winning By Design (2018).pdf, pp. 8–16).

---

jacques-attali.name: Jacques Attali
jacques-attali.eras: 20th/21st-Century French Political Economy, Critical Theory & Futurology
jacques-attali.bio:
Jacques Attali (born 1943) is a French economist, social theorist, polymath author of over eighty books, Special Adviser to President François Mitterrand (1981–1991), and founding President of the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD, 1991–1993). Educated at École Polytechnique, Sciences Po, and ENA, Attali has long investigated how cultural forms, information networks, and technological shifts prefigure macroeconomic transformations.

In his landmark treatise [[noise-the-political-economy-of-music]] (*Bruits*, 1977 / 1985), Attali argues that music is not a passive reflection of the economic base, but a prophetic herald of future social orders across four historical networks: *Sacrificing*, *Representing*, *Repeating*, and *Composing*.

---

james-bessen.name: James Bessen
james-bessen.eras: Economics of Technological Change, Labor Markets, Software Patents & AI Policy
james-bessen.bio:
James Bessen is Executive Director of the Technology & Policy Research Initiative at Boston University School of Law. Before becoming an economist, Bessen founded Bestinfo in 1983, developing the first commercial WYSIWYG desktop-publishing software for PCs.

In [[learning-by-doing-the-real-connection-between-innovation-wages-and-wealth]] (2015), Bessen proves through two centuries of economic history (from 19th-century Lowell power-loom weavers to modern bank ATMs and software workers) that major inventions only raise mass wages after decades of uncodified **'learning by doing'** and standardized skill diffusion.

---

james-ciuffetelli.name: James Ciuffetelli
james-ciuffetelli.eras: 21st-Century Private Equity Value Creation, Pricing & Exit Transformation
james-ciuffetelli.bio:
James Ciuffetelli is Co-Founder and Director of Whiteark (Melbourne, Australia), specializing in buy-and-build M&A execution, strategic pricing, commercial due diligence, and digital retooling for private-equity-backed businesses.

Co-authoring [[the-ultimate-private-equity-playbook]] (2021) with [[jo-hands]], Ciuffetelli outlines how operational discipline and digital transformation drive superior buy-and-build IRRs and strategic exits (source: BOOKS/Private Equity/Private+Equity+Playbook+-+by+Whiteark.pdf, pp. 2–16, 42–44).

---

james-e-lukaszewski.name: James E. Lukaszewski
james-e-lukaszewski.eras: Late 20th – Early 21st Century Crisis Management, Executive Advisory, and Strategic Communication
james-e-lukaszewski.bio:
**James E. Lukaszewski**, ABC, APR, Fellow PRSA, BEP, is one of the world's foremost crisis communication strategists, widely recognized across corporate, military, and government circles as *"America's Crisis Guru®"* (source: [[influencing-leaders]], About the Authors, p. 229). Founder and President of The Lukaszewski Group Division of Risdall Public Relations, he has spent nearly five decades coaching C-suite executives, generals, admirals, and corporate boards through existential crises, hostile litigation, regulatory investigations, and ethical reckonings.

Lukaszewski served for twenty-two years as an adjunct professor of strategic communication at New York University and has authored fourteen books on crisis communication, reputation recovery, and executive counseling. A recipient of the Public Relations Society of America (PRSA) **John W. Hill Award** and named among *Corporate Legal Times*' "28 Experts to Call When All Hell Breaks Loose," Lukaszewski focuses on the behavioral mechanics of how technical specialists transition from peripheral "doers" to trusted boardroom confidants. In [[influencing-leaders]] (2026), co-authored with [[helio-fred-garcia]], he codifies a career of executive advising into a step-by-step operating manual for reading leadership psychology, navigating the "No-Friendship Zone," and speaking the "Language of Done."

---

jay-abramson.name: Jay Abramson
jay-abramson.eras: 21st-Century Open Educational Resources (OER) & Undergraduate Mathematics Pedagogy
jay-abramson.bio:
Jay Abramson is Principal Lecturer in the School of Mathematics and Statistics at Arizona State University with over 33 years of precalculus teaching experience and leadership in open-access STEM curricula.

As Senior Contributing Author of OpenStax's [[precalculus-openstax]] (2017, 1,156 pp.), Abramson created a free, peer-reviewed bridge from algebraic/trigonometric functions to university calculus (source: BOOKS/Math/Precalculus-OP_9wwF7YT.pdf, pp. 3–4, 13–15).

---

jo-hands.name: Jo Hands
jo-hands.eras: 21st-Century Private Equity Operational Transformation & Commercial Strategy
jo-hands.bio:
Jo Hands is Co-Founder and Director of Whiteark (Melbourne, Australia), a management consulting and operational-transformation firm partnering with private equity sponsors and portfolio executives from acquisition due diligence through exit readiness.

In [[the-ultimate-private-equity-playbook]] (2021, co-authored with [[james-ciuffetelli]]), Hands codifies the dual-lever framework separating Strategic Multiple-Expansion levers from Operational EBITDA-Margin levers (source: BOOKS/Private Equity/Private+Equity+Playbook+-+by+Whiteark.pdf, pp. 2–6, 44).

---

jochen-pade.name: Jochen Pade
jochen-pade.eras: 21st-Century Quantum Mechanics Pedagogy & Theoretical Physics Education
jochen-pade.bio:
Jochen Pade is a physicist at the Institut für Physik, Universität Oldenburg (Germany), celebrated for his clear, model-driven approach to teaching quantum theory without obscuring conceptual foundations behind premature technical formalism.

In his two-volume Springer textbook [[quantum-mechanics-for-pedestrians]] (2nd Ed., 2018, 1,112 pp.), Pade guides learners from single-photon polarization and toy systems through tunneling, angular momentum, quantum information, relativistic quantum mechanics, and a Quantum Field Theory primer (source: BOOKS/Physics/2018_Book_QuantumMechanicsForPedestrians I.pdf, pp. 5–6, 17–22).

---

joe-beda.name: Joe Beda
joe-beda.bio:
Joe Beda is a cofounder of Kubernetes, cofounder of Heptio (acquired by VMware), and former Principal Engineer at VMware and Staff Software Engineer at Google, where he pioneered Google Compute Engine and cloud-native container orchestration.

As co-author of [[kubernetes-up-and-running]] (3rd Ed., 2022), Beda illuminates how Kubernetes decouples application teams from underlying datacenter hardware through standardized APIs and Pods (source: BOOKS/Cloud/kubernetesup&running.pdf, pp. 2, 23–35).

---

john-anthony-west.name: John Anthony West
john-anthony-west.eras: Symbolist Egyptology, Esoteric Philosophy, Sphinx Re-dating
john-anthony-west.bio:
John Anthony West (1932–2018) was an American author, lecturer, and independent Egyptologist. West was the chief proponent of the "Symbolist" school of Egyptology pioneered by French philosopher and mathematician R. A. Schwaller de Lubicz, which views Egyptian hieroglyphic culture as the inheritor of a grand sacred science rather than a primitive bronze-age animism.

In *Serpent in the Sky* (1979), West picked up Schwaller de Lubicz's observation that the Sphinx exhibits water weathering. In the early 1990s, he recruited Boston University geologist Dr. Robert Schoch to scientifically survey the monument, triggering the worldwide controversy that overturned orthodox assumptions regarding the dating of early civilization. West received an Emmy Award for the 1993 NBC documentary *The Mystery of the Sphinx*.

john-grigsby.name: John Grigsby
john-grigsby.bio: John Grigsby is a British historian, researcher, and author specializing in comparative mythology, ancient religions, and archaeoastronomy. Holding a degree in European History, Grigsby collaborated with Graham Hancock and Robert Bauval on the landmark investigative work *The Mars Mystery* (1998), focusing on cross-cultural mythological records of celestial dragon-combats and apocalyptic impacts. Grigsby subsequently authored works on Arthurian mythology and the Celtic Grail mysteries (*Warriors of the Wasteland*).

john-hunt.name: John Hunt
john-hunt.eras: 21st-Century Python 3 Software Engineering, Functional/Concurrent Architecture & Data Analytics
john-hunt.bio:
Dr. John Hunt is a technology trainer, software architect, and Managing Director of Midmarsh Technology Ltd (Chippenham, Wiltshire, UK), having authored over a dozen Springer textbooks on object-oriented and functional programming.

In the two-volume 2019 Springer *Undergraduate Topics in Computer Science* treatise—*A Beginners Guide to Python 3 Programming* (441 pp., `DOI: 10.1007/978-3-030-20290-3`) and *Advanced Guide to Python 3 Programming* (494 pp., `DOI: 10.1007/978-3-030-25943-3`), synthesized in [[python-and-r-scientific-computing-foundations-for-ai-and-data-science]]—Hunt covers the complete Python 3 ecosystem from object-oriented design, closures, currying, and metaclasses to Matplotlib/Seaborn visualization, SQL/NoSQL databases, asyncio/multiprocessing concurrency, and reactive programming (source: BOOKS/AI/2019_Book_ABeginnersGuideToPython3Progra.pdf, pp. 1–9; BOOKS/AI/2019_Book_AdvancedGuideToPython3Programm.pdf, pp. 1–9).

---

john-keane.name: John Keane
john-keane.eras: 21st-Century Global Democratic Theory & Post-Westminster Institutional Analysis
john-keane.bio:
**John Keane** is Professor of Politics at the University of Sydney and at the Wissenschaftszentrum Berlin (WZB), founder of the Centre for the Study of Democracy in London, and one of the world's foremost historians and theorists of democracy. In his monumental work [[the-life-and-death-of-democracy-and-monitory-democracy]] (*The Life and Death of Democracy*, 2009—also featured in Chapter 14 of [[the-secret-history-of-democracy-primitive-democracy]]), Keane wrote the first full-scale global history of democracy in over a century (source: [[the-life-and-death-of-democracy-and-monitory-democracy]], pp. 1–2).

Keane traces democracy across three historical epochs: **Assembly Democracy** (originating c. 2500 BC in ancient Syria-Mesopotamia before moving westward to Phoenicia and Greece), **Representative Democracy** (parliamentary and constitutional territorial states from the medieval era through the Atlantic revolutions), and **Monitory Democracy**—a post-1945 paradigm coined by Keane in which periodic ballot-box elections are embedded within a dense web of extra-parliamentary **"watchdog" institutions** (constitutional courts, human rights commissions, integrity auditors, citizen assemblies, and digital investigative media) that subject political and corporate power to continuous public scrutiny.

---

john-sanei.name: John Sanei
john-sanei.eras: 21st-Century Futures Strategy, Applied Neuroscience, and Adaptive Leadership
john-sanei.bio:
**John Sanei** is a South African-born global futures strategist, bestselling author, and leadership educator who combines future studies, consumer behavior, and applied neuroscience to help individuals and organizations navigate exponential disruption (source: [[the-adaptability-advantage]], Introduction & About the Author, pp. 13–17, 187). He serves as a faculty member at **Singularity University** in Silicon Valley and as an associate lecturer at **Duke Corporate Education (Duke CE)**, and was the first African invited to join the global Singularity University faculty.

Co-host of the award-winning *The Expansive* podcast and author of ten books (including *What's Your Moonshot?* and *Who Do We Become?*), Sanei argues that traditional strategic planning fails during civilizational transitions because leaders attempt to solve novel futures using survival-wired, past-conditioned nervous systems. In [[the-adaptability-advantage]] (2026), he synthesizes trauma release, neuroplasticity, emotional mastery, and technological foresight into a six-part blueprint—teaching leaders how to clear **Emotional Debt**, cultivate **Adaptive Intelligence (AQ)**, and balance high-tech artificial intelligence with high-touch human wisdom.

---

jonas-hubotter.name: Jonas Hübotter
jonas-hubotter.eras: 21st-Century Probabilistic AI, Active Learning & Sequential Decision-Making
jonas-hubotter.bio:
Jonas Hübotter is a machine learning researcher at the Institute for Machine Learning, Department of Computer Science, ETH Zürich, specializing in information-directed active learning, test-time adaptation, and sequential decision-making under uncertainty.

Co-authoring [[probabilistic-artificial-intelligence]] (2025) with [[andreas-krause]], Hübotter develops the pedagogical synthesis bridging variational/MCMC posterior approximation with active data acquisition and constrained exploration in reinforcement learning (source: BOOKS/AI/2025 Probabilistic AI.pdf, pp. 1–10, 157–298).

---

jonathan-haidt.name: Jonathan Haidt
jonathan-haidt.eras: Moral Psychology, Institutional Pluralism, and Digital-Age Social Psychology
jonathan-haidt.bio:
**Jonathan Haidt, PhD**, is the Thomas Cooley Professor of Ethical Leadership at the **New York University Stern School of Business** (source: [[leading-for-tomorrow]], Chapter 23 & Contributors, pp. 281–291, 330). Earning his BA in philosophy from Yale University and his PhD in social psychology from the University of Pennsylvania, Haidt taught for sixteen years at the University of Virginia before joining NYU Stern. Named one of *Foreign Policy*'s "Top 100 Global Thinkers" and *Prospect* magazine's "Top World Thinkers," he is co-founder of Heterodox Academy, the Constructive Dialogue Institute, and EthicalSystems.org.

Co-architect of **Moral Foundations Theory**, Haidt is the author of several widely influential books, including *The Happiness Hypothesis* (2006), *The Righteous Mind: Why Good People Are Divided by Politics and Religion* (2012), *The Coddling of the American Mind* (2018, with Greg Lukianoff), and the #1 *New York Times* bestseller *The Anxious Generation* (2024). In Chapter 23 of [[leading-for-tomorrow]] (2026), Haidt analyzes how the "Great Rewiring of Childhood" (the shift from a play-based to a phone-based childhood between 2010 and 2015) and hyper-polarized social media ecosystems have reshaped the incoming workforce, urging leaders to restore institutional telos (truth vs. social advocacy), foster viewpoint diversity, and rebuild resilient, high-trust workplace norms.

---

jorg-noll.name: Jörg Noll
jorg-noll.bio:
Dr. Jörg Noll is Assistant Professor of Military Operational Art and Science at the Faculty of Military Sciences, Netherlands Defence Academy (NLDA). He specializes in contemporary deterrence operations, NATO forward deployments, and conflict stability in Eastern Europe.

In *Deterrence in the 21st Century*, Noll (with Osman Bojang and Sebastiaan Rietjens) authored Chapter 7 ("Deterrence by Punishment or Denial? The eFP Case"), evaluating NATO's enhanced Forward Presence battlegroups in the Baltic states and Poland.

---
jorg-noll.recurring_themes:
- [[deterrence-and-coercion]]: Tripwire forces, deterrence by denial versus punishment.
- [[military-science]]: Forward deployment and multinational interoperability.

josh-kosman.name: Josh Kosman
josh-kosman.eras: 21st-Century Investigative Financial Journalism & Wall Street LBO Critique
josh-kosman.bio:
Josh Kosman is an investigative business journalist who covered leveraged buyouts and M&A for *Buyouts Newsletter*, *The Deal*, *Mergermarket* (where he headed North American operations), and the *New York Post* after beginning his career at the Warburg Pincus–acquired *Middletown Press*.

In [[the-buyout-of-america]] (2009), Kosman exposes the debt-loading mechanics, dividend recapitalizations, service cuts, and systemic credit-crisis hazards of the 2001–2007 private equity buyout boom (source: BOOKS/Private Equity/2009 The_Buyout_of_America_-_Josh_Kosman.pdf, pp. 9–15).

---

joyce-kay-avila.name: Joyce Kay Avila
joyce-kay-avila.eras: 21st-Century Cloud Data Warehousing, Data Engineering & Governance
joyce-kay-avila.bio:
Joyce Kay Avila is a Snowflake Data Superhero, Snowflake consulting practice manager, certified public accountant (CPA), MBA, and computer scientist who completed PhD coursework in accounting information systems.

In [[snowflake-the-definitive-guide]] (2022), Avila delivers an authoritative end-to-end engineering guide to Snowflake's three-layer decoupled architecture, virtual warehouses, Streams/Tasks, RBAC governance, Zero-Copy Cloning, Time Travel, and Secure Data Sharing (source: BOOKS/Cloud/Snowflake-The-Definitive-Guide-1.pdf, pp. 2, 16, 48–255).

---

judith-hurwitz.name: Judith Hurwitz
judith-hurwitz.eras: 21st-Century Cognitive Computing, Enterprise Cloud & Machine Learning Strategy
judith-hurwitz.bio:
Judith Hurwitz is a technology strategist, corporate advisor, and President of Hurwitz & Associates, having co-authored over ten Wiley *For Dummies* enterprise computing guides including *Cognitive Computing and Big Data Analytics*.

In [[machine-learning-for-dummies-ibm-limited-edition]] (John Wiley & Sons, 2018, 75 pp., co-authored with [[daniel-kirsch]]), Hurwitz provides an executive and practitioner guide to transitioning from static rule-based software to dynamic, data-driven machine learning lifecycles (source: BOOKS/AI/2017 Book ML for Dummies by IBM_.pdf, pp. 1–16, 27–36).

---

junfeng-yang.name: Junfeng Yang
junfeng-yang.eras: Smart Classrooms, Learner Experience (LX) & Digital Pedagogy
junfeng-yang.bio:
Junfeng Yang is Professor of Educational Technology at the School of Education, Hangzhou Normal University (China), specializing in smart learning environments and learner experience evaluation.

In [[educational-technology-a-primer-for-the-21st-century]] (2019), co-authored with [[ronghuai-huang]] and [[j-michael-spector]], Yang develops the Learner Experience (LX) indicators and technology integration frameworks.

---

karen-hao.name: Karen Hao
karen-hao.eras: 21st-Century Investigative Technology Journalism & Political Economy of AI
karen-hao.bio:
Karen Hao is an award-winning investigative journalist and former senior AI editor at *MIT Technology Review*, foreign correspondent for *The Wall Street Journal*, and contributor to *The Atlantic*.

Drawing on seven years of reporting and over 300 interviews with more than 260 insiders—including 90+ current and former OpenAI executives, researchers, and contractors alongside field investigations across Kenya, Chile, and Uruguay—Hao authored [[empire-of-ai-dreams-and-nightmares-in-sam-altmans-openai]] (Penguin Press, 2025, 575 pp.), dissecting how OpenAI transformed from a non-profit safety lab into an imperial corporate apparatus (source: BOOKS/AI/2025 empire-of-ai-dreams-and-nightmares-in-sam-altmans-openai.pdf, pp. 3–11, 25–26, 251).

---

karen-scarfone.name: Karen Scarfone
karen-scarfone.eras: NIST Cybersecurity Guidelines & Enterprise Security Architecture
karen-scarfone.bio:
Karen Scarfone is the Principal Cybersecurityister and Founder of Scarfone Cybersecurity and a former Senior Computer Scientist at NIST, where she authored or co-authored more than fifty NIST Special Publications and Interagency Reports on intrusion detection, firewalls, vulnerability management, and incident response.

In [[computer-security-incident-handling-guide-nist-sp-800-61r2]], Scarfone co-authored the technical detection, precursor/indicator analysis, and recovery guidelines.

---

karl-mueller.name: Karl Mueller
karl-mueller.eras: Contemporary [[strategic-studies]], Conventional Deterrence Theory, Air Power Strategy
karl-mueller.bio:
Karl P. Mueller is a Senior Political Scientist at the RAND Corporation and former Professor of Comparative Military Studies at the US Air Force School of Advanced Air and Space Studies (SAASS). Mueller holds a Ph.D. in Politics from Princeton University and is recognized internationally for his foundational scholarship on conventional deterrence, coercive air power, and strategic escalation.

In *Deterrence in the 21st Century*, Mueller authored Chapter 4 ("The Continuing Relevance of Conventional Deterrence"), categorizing conventional deterrence into four distinct operational and geographic modes and analyzing why conventional deterrence poses different structural and cognitive challenges than nuclear deterrence.

---
karl-mueller.recurring_themes:
- [[deterrence-and-coercion]]: Conventional deterrence by denial versus punishment.
- [[military-science]]: Operational art, conventional force posture, and escalation thresholds.
- [[strategic-studies]]: Historical analysis of deterrence successes and failures.

kelsey-hightower.name: Kelsey Hightower
kelsey-hightower.bio:
