Kelsey Hightower is a renowned distributed-systems engineer, open-source leader, and longtime Principal Engineer and Developer Advocate in Google's cloud computing division celebrated for minimalist, hands-on operational leadership and teaching cloud-native infrastructure.

In [[kubernetes-up-and-running]] (3rd Ed., 2022), Hightower brings production-hardened pragmatism to cluster lifecycle management, Pods, Services, RBAC security, and real-world deployments (source: BOOKS/Cloud/kubernetesup&running.pdf, pp. 2, 69–124).

---

kenneth-i-carlaw.name: Kenneth I. Carlaw
kenneth-i-carlaw.eras: Evolutionary Macroeconomics, Endogenous GPT Modeling & Innovation Policy
kenneth-i-carlaw.bio:
Kenneth I. Carlaw is Professor of Economics at the University of British Columbia (Okanagan), specializing in formal simulation models of endogenous technological change, Total Factor Productivity (TFP) critique, and General Purpose Technologies.

In [[economic-transformations-general-purpose-technologies-and-long-term-economic-growth]] (2005), co-authored with [[richard-g-lipsey]] and [[clifford-t-bekar]], Carlaw develops the non-stationary three-sector GPT growth models and proves why TFP fails to measure technological change.

---

kent-d-lee.name: Kent D. Lee
kent-d-lee.eras: 21st-Century Computer Science Pedagogy, Debugger-Driven Learning & Computational Complexity
kent-d-lee.bio:
Prof. Kent D. Lee is Professor of Computer Science at Luther College (Decorah, Iowa), author of Springer textbooks on Python, data structures, and programming languages.

In *Python Programming Fundamentals (Second Edition)* (Springer *Undergraduate Topics in Computer Science*, 2014, 241 pp., `DOI: 10.1007/978-1-4471-6642-9`, synthesized in [[python-and-r-scientific-computing-foundations-for-ai-and-data-science]]), Lee pioneers debugger-driven computer science pedagogy, teaching students to inspect execution stack frames, recursion, object-oriented Tkinter GUIs, and algorithmic complexity from day one (source: BOOKS/AI/2014_Book_PythonProgrammingFundamentals.pdf, pp. 1–8).

---

kerri-oneill.name: Kerri O'Neill
kerri-oneill.eras: Contemporary People Strategy, AI Workplace Transformation, and Organizational Rewilding
kerri-oneill.bio:
**Kerri O'Neill** is Chief People Officer for **Ipsos UK & Ireland**, Global Lead for AI Workplace Transformation at Ipsos, and a Trustee of **Oxfam GB** (source: [[rapid-reculturing]], About the Authors, pp. 295–296). Named to the **CIPD HR30** list of the most influential human resources leaders and recipient of multiple industry awards for workplace culture and inclusion, O'Neill has led global people transformations across media, market research, retail, and international humanitarian organizations.

Previously serving as Senior Partner at Bailey & French alongside [[alex-bailey]], O'Neill bridges theoretical organizational psychology with frontline executive execution across hybrid workforces and AI-disrupted industries. In [[rapid-reculturing]] (2026), co-authored with Bailey, she documents how organizations can dismantle bureaucratic friction ("process debt"), deploy the **5-5-5 Coaching Conversation**, and integrate generative AI as an empowering human co-pilot rather than an instrument of surveillance.

---

kevin-mcginley.name: Kevin McGinley
kevin-mcginley.eras: 21st-Century Cloud Data Engineering & SaaS Analytics Architecture
kevin-mcginley.bio:
Kevin McGinley is a veteran data-analytics architect and Snowflake technical leader specializing in modern cloud data warehousing, embedded analytics, and Customer 360 platforms.

As co-author of [[architecting-data-intensive-saas-applications]] (2021), McGinley details how SaaS product teams offload infrastructure management onto multi-cloud data platforms to accelerate customer-facing analytics (source: BOOKS/SaaS/OReilly-Report-Architecting-Data-Intensive-SaaS-Applications.pdf, pp. 3–4, 7–30).

---

kim-richard-nossal.name: Kim Richard Nossal
kim-richard-nossal.eras: Contemporary Canadian Foreign & Defense Policy and International Relations
kim-richard-nossal.bio:
**Kim Richard Nossal** is Professor Emeritus of Political Studies and former Director of the Centre for International and Defence Policy at **Queen's University** (and former Head of Political Science at McMaster University), widely recognized as a dean of Canadian foreign and defense policy studies. As co-editor of [[developing-the-super-soldier-enhancing-military-performance]] (*Developing the Super Soldier: Enhancing Military Performance*, 2017, with [[william-g-braun-iii]] and [[stefanie-von-hlatky]]), Nossal examines the institutional, political, and ethical governance of military performance enhancement across Western allied armed forces (source: [[developing-the-super-soldier-enhancing-military-performance]], pp. 1–6, viii).

---

kurt-and-margot-lubinski.name: Kurt & Margot Lubinski
kurt-and-margot-lubinski.eras: Early 20th-Century Photojournalism / Weimar & National Geographic Ethnographic Photography
kurt-and-margot-lubinski.bio:
Kurt Lubinski (1899–1969) and Margot Lubinski (née Lewin) were German-Jewish photojournalists and ethnographic photographers who traveled extensively across Europe, Anatolia, Central Asia, and Ethiopia in the late 1920s and 1930s before emigrating from Nazi Germany to the Netherlands, London, and New York. Contributing to *National Geographic* and international illustrated weeklies, their candid street photography documented societies undergoing rapid modernization.

In [[gormedigimiz-turkiye-123-yillik-national-geographic-arsivi]], their September 1933 photographs of Ankara on the eve of the Turkish Republic's tenth anniversary capture the optimism, civic conviviality, and everyday urban life of early Republican citizens.

---

kwo-young.name: Kwo Young
kwo-young.eras: Electrochemical Battery Engineering & Electric Vehicle Powertrain Systems
kwo-young.bio:
Dr. Kwo Young is a principal battery materials scientist at BASF / Ovonic Battery Company who has authored numerous foundational studies on Nickel-Metal Hydride (NiMH) and Lithium-ion (Li-ion) electrochemistry for hybrid and battery electric vehicles.

In [[electric-vehicles-light-duty-fuel-economy-and-shared-micromobility]], Young (with Caisheng Wang, Le Yi Wang, and Kai Strunz) formulates the propulsion physics, State of Charge ($SOC$) / Depth of Discharge ($DOD$) dynamics, and cell-voltage vs. safety trade-offs of EV battery packs.

---

lachlan-evenson.name: Lachlan Evenson
lachlan-evenson.bio:
Lachlan Evenson is a Principal Product Manager on Microsoft Azure's container compute team and a Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) ambassador who has guided thousands of practitioners into Kubernetes adoption through hands-on engineering education.

Joining the Third Edition of [[kubernetes-up-and-running]] (2022), Evenson helped expand the manual to cover modern Container Runtime Interfaces, Ingress controllers, extensibility, and multicluster deployments (source: BOOKS/Cloud/kubernetesup&running.pdf, pp. 2, 6, 23–123).

---

lane-denicola.name: Lane DeNicola
lane-denicola.eras: 21st-Century Digital Anthropology, Design Ethnography, STS & Geomedia
lane-denicola.bio:
Lane DeNicola is an anthropologist and Science and Technology Studies (STS) scholar researching geospatial information systems, satellite imaging, ubiquitous computing, and the intersection of ethnography and industrial interaction design.

In [[the-digital-as-para-world]] (2011) and his *Geomedia* chapter in [[digital-anthropology]] (2012), DeNicola frames digital technologies as a 'para-world' intersecting pre-existing physical spaces and social orders (source: BOOKS/Anthropology_/denicola-in-clarke The Digital as Para-world.pdf, pp. 1–2).

---

laura-igual.name: Laura Igual
laura-igual.eras: 21st-Century Python Data Science, Computer Vision & Statistical Modeling
laura-igual.bio:
Dr. Laura Igual is Associate Professor in the Department of Mathematics and Computer Science at the Universitat de Barcelona (Spain) and researcher at the Computer Vision Center (CVC).

In [[introduction-to-data-science-a-python-approach-to-concepts-techniques-and-applications]] (Springer *Undergraduate Topics in Computer Science*, 2017, 227 pp., `DOI: 10.1007/978-3-319-50017-1`, co-authored with [[santi-segui]]), Igual synthesizes the complete Python data-science workflow—from Pandas/NumPy exploratory data analysis, statistical estimation, and LASSO sparse regression to network analysis, recommender systems, A/B testing, and MapReduce big-data pipelines (source: BOOKS/AI/2017_Book_IntroductionToDataScience.pdf, pp. 1–11, 51, 121, 181).

---

lawrence-c-miller.name: Lawrence C. Miller
lawrence-c-miller.eras: 21st-Century Enterprise Cloud, IoT Architecture & Information Security Education
lawrence-c-miller.bio:
Lawrence C. Miller, CISSP, is a prolific enterprise technology author, information-security specialist, and veteran contributor to John Wiley & Sons' *For Dummies* Custom Publishing series across IoT, cloud infrastructure, cybersecurity, and enterprise SaaS.

Across five Wiley Special Editions in this wiki—the three-volume [[iot-for-dummies-applications-solutions-and-security-compendium]] (2016–2018, for INSIDE Secure, Qorvo, and Arm), [[iaas-for-dummies-oracle-special-edition]] (2018), and [[saas-for-dummies-oracle-special-edition]] (2021)—Miller maps the full enterprise modernization stack from hardware-rooted edge security to second-generation bare-metal IaaS and AI-embedded cloud SaaS suites (source: BOOKS/IoT/Book IoT_Security_for_Dummies_VNK.pdf, pp. 3–7; BOOKS/Cloud/Book IaaS_For_Dummies_2nd_Oracle_Special_Edition.pdf, pp. 3–11; BOOKS/SaaS/saas-for-dummies-3rdedition.pdf, pp. 3–7).

---

lawrence-freedman.name: Lawrence Freedman
lawrence-freedman.eras: Modern [[strategic-studies]], Nuclear Strategy History, Strategic Theory
lawrence-freedman.bio:
Sir Lawrence Freedman (born 1948) is Professor Emeritus of War Studies at King's College London, widely regarded as the dean of modern British strategic studies. Knighted in 2003 and appointed to the UK Privy Council in 2009 (where he served on the Chilcot Inquiry into the Iraq War), Freedman is the author of classic works including *The Evolution of Nuclear Strategy* (1981), *Strategy: A History* (2013), and *The Future of War: A History* (2017).

In *Deterrence in the 21st Century*, Freedman contributed the introductory chapter tracing the conceptual history of deterrence research through its major historical waves—from the early nuclear revolution to contemporary multi-domain deterrence.

---
lawrence-freedman.recurring_themes:
- [[deterrence-and-coercion]]: The conceptual evolution, limits, and enduring utility of deterrence.
- [[nuclear-strategy-and-strategic-stability]]: The history and paradoxes of nuclear doctrine and extended deterrence.
- [[rationality-and-decision-making]]: The gap between abstract strategic theories and the political-operational realities of military decision-makers.

learningexpress-editors.name: LearningExpress Skill Builder Writing Team
learningexpress-editors.bio:
The LearningExpress Skill Builder in Focus Writing Team comprises practicing middle-school, high-school, and college mathematics and literacy educators dedicated to structured self-study problem mastery.

Their workbook *501 Math Word Problems* (2003, paired with [[alex-oconnor]] in [[501-math-word-problems-and-middle-school-math-challenges]]) trains systematic real-world translation across fractions, percents, algebra, and geometry (source: BOOKS/Math/MathWorldProblems.pdf, pp. 5–8).

---

leonard-mlodinow.name: Leonard Mlodinow
leonard-mlodinow.eras: 21st-Century Theoretical Physics, Probability & Popular Philosophy of Science
leonard-mlodinow.bio:
Leonard Mlodinow is a Caltech-affiliated theoretical physicist and bestselling science author (*The Drunkard's Walk*, *Euclid's Window*, *Feynman's Rainbow*) who collaborated closely with [[stephen-hawking]] on *A Briefer History of Time* and *The Grand Design*.

In [[the-grand-design]] (2010, co-authored with [[stephen-hawking]]), Mlodinow articulates Model-Dependent Realism, Feynman sum-over-histories cosmology, and the M-theory multiverse (source: BOOKS/Physics/The Grand Design ( PDFDrive ).pdf, pp. 2, 6, 10, 37).

---

leopold-aschenbrenner.name: Leopold Aschenbrenner
leopold-aschenbrenner.eras: 21st-Century AGI Scaling Theory, Superalignment & National Security Mobilization
leopold-aschenbrenner.bio:
Leopold Aschenbrenner graduated as valedictorian of Columbia University at age 19, served on OpenAI's Superalignment team under Ilya Sutskever and Jan Leike until 2024, and subsequently founded the San Francisco macro-technology investment fund Situational Awareness LP.

In his landmark June 2024 monograph [[situational-awareness-the-decade-ahead]] (165 pp., dedicated to Ilya Sutskever), Aschenbrenner extrapolates compute, algorithmic, and 'unhobbling' orders of magnitude (OOMs) to argue that AGI by 2027 is strikingly plausible, that automated AI research will trigger a rapid intelligence explosion to superintelligence, and that a Manhattan Project–scale U.S. national security mobilization ('The Project') is inevitable (source: BOOKS/AI/2024 Situational_Awareness_Leopold_Aschenbrenner.pdf, pp. 1–6, 41, 81, 121–151).

---

louise-bennett.name: Louise Bennett (Miss Lou)
louise-bennett.eras: 20th-Century Jamaican Creole Poetry, Caribbean Oral Tradition & Postcolonial Literature
louise-bennett.bio:
Louise Simone Bennett-Coverley, OM, OJ, MBE (1919–2006), affectionately known as **'Miss Lou,'** was a pioneering Jamaican poet, folklorist, educator, and BBC radio host (* Caribbean Carnival*, 1945–1953) who elevated Jamaican Patois ('Nation Language') from colonial stigmatization to a celebrated literary art form.

As analyzed by [[ashley-dawson]] in [[mongrel-nation-colonization-in-reverse]], Bennett's famous dramatic monologue *'Colonization in Reverse'* satirized and celebrated the post-1948 Windrush exodus to Britain as a world-historical inversion of the British Empire.

---

marc-benioff.name: Marc Benioff
marc-benioff.eras: 21st-Century Cloud Computing, Enterprise SaaS & Stakeholder Capitalism
marc-benioff.bio:
Marc Benioff is the cofounder, Chair, and CEO of Salesforce (founded in 1999 after a 13-year executive career at Oracle), widely credited as the chief evangelist of Software-as-a-Service (SaaS), multi-tenant cloud CRM, the V2MOM management framework, and the 1-1-1 integrated corporate philanthropy model.

In [[behind-the-cloud]] (2009, co-authored with [[carlye-adler]]), Benioff shares 111 operational plays detailing how Salesforce's 'End of Software' campaign scaled from a San Francisco apartment into a global cloud platform (source: BOOKS/SaaS/Behind the Cloud_ The Untold Story of How Salesforce.com Went from Idea to Billion-Dollar Company-and Revolutionized an Industry   ( PDFDrive ).pdf, pp. 2–6, 10–15).

---

marco-di-maggio.name: Marco Di Maggio
marco-di-maggio.eras: 21st-Century Financial Economics, FinTech, Cryptoeconomics & Decentralized Finance
marco-di-maggio.bio:
Marco Di Maggio is a Professor at Harvard Business School and Imperial College Business School, Faculty Research Fellow at the National Bureau of Economic Research (NBER), and Co-Director of the HBS FinTech Lab. His scholarship spans financial intermediation, monetary policy transmission, credit networks, decentralized finance (DeFi), and Web3 tokenomics.

In [[blockchain-crypto-and-defi-bridging-finance-and-technology]], Di Maggio synthesizes the cryptographic foundations, smart-contract architectures, Layer-2 scaling, stablecoins, CBDCs, Automated Market Makers, regulatory frameworks, and AI-blockchain convergence shaping modern digital finance.

---

mark-b-houston.name: Mark B. Houston
mark-b-houston.eras: Marketing Strategy, Entertainment Econometrics & Innovation Management
mark-b-houston.bio:
Mark B. Houston is the Eunice and James L. West Chair in Marketing at the Neeley School of Business, Texas Christian University, and former Editor-in-Chief of the *Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science*.

In [[entertainment-science-data-analytics-and-practical-theory]] (2019), co-authored with [[thorsten-hennig-thurau]], Houston synthesizes 35 years of empirical research across movies, games, books, and music.

---

marshall-s-rich.name: Marshall S. Rich
marshall-s-rich.eras: 21st-Century Forensic Cyberpsychology, Behavioral Network Forensics & AI Security
marshall-s-rich.bio:
Dr. Marshall S. Rich holds a PhD in Forensic Cyberpsychology and is a cybersecurity researcher and practitioner specializing in the intersection of network forensics, machine learning anomaly detection, and behavioral profiling of cyber adversaries.

In [[advanced-network-forensics-a-cyber-behavioral-science-approach]] (2026), Rich introduces the **Cyber Forensics Behavioral Analysis (CFBA)** model and **Adversarial Behavioral Score (ABS)**, uniting Dark Triad/Big Five psychological profiling with deception networks and SCADA/IoT critical infrastructure forensics.

---

martijn-kitzen.name: Martijn Kitzen
martijn-kitzen.bio:
Prof. Dr. Martijn Kitzen holds the Chair of Irregular Warfare and Special Operations at the Faculty of Military Sciences, Netherlands Defence Academy (NLDA). A former Royal Netherlands Army infantry officer with operational deployments, Kitzen specializes in local conflict dynamics, tribal networks, and counterinsurgency.

In *Deterrence in the 21st Century*, Kitzen (with Christina van Kuijck) authored Chapter 15 ("All Deterrence Is Local: The Utility and Application of Localised Deterrence in Counterinsurgency"), demonstrating how micro-level social dynamics govern deterrence in irregular conflicts.

---
martijn-kitzen.recurring_themes:
- [[violent-non-state-actors]]: Granular village-level deterrence and population-centric security.
- [[military-science]]: Irregular warfare and counterinsurgency operational design.

matt-lucas.name: Matt Lucas
matt-lucas.eras: Enterprise Blockchain Strategy & Supply Chain Digitization
matt-lucas.bio:
Matt Lucas is an enterprise blockchain leader at IBM who has guided Fortune 500 consortia across trade finance, supply chain provenance, and financial services.

In [[getting-started-with-enterprise-blockchain]], Lucas details use-case qualification, business network incentives, and consortium operating models.

---

matthew-dixon.name: Matthew Dixon
matthew-dixon.eras: 21st-Century B2B Commercial Research, Challenger Selling & Customer Experience
matthew-dixon.bio:
Matthew Dixon is a business researcher, founding partner of DCM Insights, and former Executive Director at the Corporate Executive Board (CEB, now Gartner), where he co-authored *The Challenger Sale* (2011), *The Effortless Experience* (2013), *The Challenger Customer* (2015), and *The JOLT Effect* (2022).

In [[the-challenger-sale-challenge-yourself-action-book]] (2021), Dixon and [[brent-adamson]]'s empirical research demonstrates how top B2B advisors win by **Teaching for Differentiation**, **Tailoring for Resonance**, **Taking Control**, and calibrating **Constructive Tension**.

---

matthew-golby-kirk.name: Matthew Golby-Kirk
matthew-golby-kirk.eras: Enterprise Software Architecture & Smart Contract Engineering
matthew-golby-kirk.bio:
Matthew Golby-Kirk is a software architect and blockchain educator at IBM specializing in smart contract (chaincode) lifecycle management, DevOps, and cloud deployment.

In [[getting-started-with-enterprise-blockchain]], Golby-Kirk co-authors the practical design and development guides for enterprise distributed ledgers.

---

max-smeets.name: Max Smeets
max-smeets.eras: Cyber Strategy, National Cyber Power, Transatlantic Tech Policy
max-smeets.bio:
Dr. Max Smeets is Director of the European Cyber Conflict Research Initiative (ECCRI) and Senior Researcher at the Center for Security Studies (CSS) at ETH Zurich. He is an Affiliate at Stanford University's CISAC and author of *No Shortcuts: Why States Struggle to Develop a Military Cyber-Force*.

In *Deterrence in the 21st Century*, Smeets (with Stefan Soesanto) authored Chapter 20 ("Cyber Deterrence: The Past, Present, and Future"), evaluating how the unique technical properties of cyberspace reshape deterrence theory.

---
max-smeets.recurring_themes:
- [[hybrid-threats-and-cyber-warfare]]: The limitations of cyber deterrence by punishment and denial.
- [[cross-domain-conflict]]: Cyber capabilities as instruments of strategic bargaining.

max-solomon-bennett.name: Max Solomon Bennett
max-solomon-bennett.eras: 21st-Century Evolutionary Neuroscience, Cognitive Science & AI Architecture
max-solomon-bennett.bio:
Max Solomon Bennett is an AI researcher, cognitive neuroscience writer, and entrepreneur (co-founder of Alby and former VP of Product at Bluecore) whose work bridges evolutionary neurobiology and artificial intelligence.

In [[a-brief-history-of-intelligence-evolution-ai-and-the-five-breakthroughs-that-made-our-brains]] (2023/2025, 103 pp. synthesis edition), Bennett reconstructs the four-billion-year evolutionary lineage of the human brain through five canonical architectural breakthroughs—*Steering*, *Reinforcing*, *Simulating*, *Mentalizing*, and *Speaking*—and maps each directly onto modern AI paradigms on the threshold of 'Breakthrough #6' (silicon superintelligence) (source: BOOKS/AI/2025 A Brief History of Intelligence.pdf, pp. 3–11, 31, 91).

---

mehmet-eroz.name: Mehmet Eröz
mehmet-eroz.eras: 20th-Century Turkish Sociology, Anatolian Ethnography & Economic History
mehmet-eroz.bio:
Prof. Dr. Mehmet Eröz (1930–1986, born in Söke, Aydın) was a pioneering Turkish sociologist and ethnographer at Istanbul University's Faculty of Economics who earned his PhD (1965) on Yörük socio-economic organization, his docentship (1971) on Marxist critique, and his professorship (1977) on Alevism and Bektashism.

In his classic posthumous monograph [[yorukler]] (1991), Eröz preserves primary highland (*yayla*) fieldwork documenting the social, religious, linguistic, and pastoral-economic institutions of Anatolia's nomadic Turkish tribes (source: BOOKS/Anthropology_/Yorukler_Mehmet_Eroz.pdf, pp. 2, 7–10).

---

michael-b-horn.name: Michael B. Horn
michael-b-horn.eras: Disruptive Innovation in Education, Blended Learning & Student-Centered Schooling
michael-b-horn.bio:
Michael B. Horn is the co-founder of and Distinguished Fellow at the Clayton Christensen Institute for Disruptive Innovation, Lecturer at the Harvard Graduate School of Education, and a leading architect of competency-based and blended K–12 and higher education reform.

As co-author of [[disrupting-class-how-disruptive-innovation-will-change-the-way-the-world-learns]] (2008) with [[clayton-m-christensen]] and [[curtis-w-johnson]] and lead co-author of [[blended-using-disruptive-innovation-to-improve-schools]] (2015) with [[heather-staker]], Horn established the global taxonomy of blended learning (**Rotation, Flex, A La Carte, Enriched Virtual**) and applied **Jobs-to-Be-Done** to student motivation.

---

michael-bhaskar.name: Michael Bhaskar
michael-bhaskar.eras: 21st-Century Publishing Theory, Curation Economics & Technology Policy
michael-bhaskar.bio:
Michael Bhaskar is a British writer, researcher, and publishing entrepreneur (co-founder of Canelo and former Writer-in-Residence at DeepMind), known for *The Content Machine* (2013), *Curation* (2016), and *Human Frontiers* (2021).

Co-authoring [[the-coming-wave-ai-power-and-our-future]] (2023) with [[mustafa-suleyman]], Bhaskar situates the AI and synthetic biology supercluster within the macro-history of general-purpose technological waves and the fragility of the modern nation-state (source: BOOKS/AI/The Coming Wave_ AI, Power, and Our Future - Notebook.html, Ch. 2–12, pp. 37–276).

---

michael-bradley.name: Michael Bradley
michael-bradley.eras: Enterprise Distributed Ledger Architecture & IBM Blockchain Engineering
michael-bradley.bio:
Michael Bradley is the Global Program Director for Blockchain Enablement and Education at IBM, with over two decades of enterprise architecture experience across IBM Development Labs (Messaging, IoT, Emerging Technologies) and IBM Services.

As lead co-author of [[getting-started-with-enterprise-blockchain]] alongside [[david-gorman]], [[matt-lucas]], and [[matthew-golby-kirk]], Bradley codifies the governance, PKI privacy, and Hyperledger Fabric smart-contract patterns for permissioned multi-company business networks.

---

michael-mazarr.name: Michael J. Mazarr
michael-mazarr.eras: Contemporary [[strategic-studies]], Defense Policy Analysis, Deterrence Theory
michael-mazarr.bio:
Michael J. Mazarr is a Senior Political Scientist at the RAND Corporation and former Associate Dean and Professor of Strategy at the US National War College. Mazarr has authored numerous influential studies for the US Department of Defense and Joint Staff on grand strategy, grey-zone conflict, deterrence dynamics, and international order.

In *Deterrence in the 21st Century*, Mazarr authored Chapter 2 ("Understanding Deterrence"), providing a comprehensive foundation of core deterrence principles: the distinction between deterrence by denial and deterrence by punishment, the essential role of assurances, and the cognitive requirements for credible signaling.

---
michael-mazarr.recurring_themes:
- [[deterrence-and-coercion]]: Core mechanisms of denial, punishment, and the crucial necessity of credible assurances.
- [[rationality-and-decision-making]]: Perception, miscalculation, and psychological factors in crisis deterrence.
- [[hybrid-threats-and-cyber-warfare]]: Deterring sub-threshold and grey-zone aggression.

michael-prahl.name: Michael Prahl
michael-prahl.eras: 21st-Century Global Private Equity, Cross-Border Buyouts & Fund Management
michael-prahl.bio:
Michael Prahl is a private equity practitioner, former Executive Director of INSEAD's Global Private Equity Initiative (GPEI), and co-founder of Asia-focused private equity advisory and investment ventures.

Co-authoring [[mastering-private-equity]] (2017) with [[claudia-zeisberger]] and [[bowen-white]], Prahl bridges academic corporate finance with real-world deal sourcing, auction pricing, governance, and operational transformation (source: BOOKS/Private Equity/2017 mastering-private-equity-transformation-via-venture-capital-minority-investments-and-buyouts.pdf, pp. 5–7, 346).

---

michael-wooldridge.name: Michael Wooldridge
michael-wooldridge.eras: Late 20th & 21st-Century Multi-Agent Systems, Autonomous Rational Agents & AI History
michael-wooldridge.bio:
Michael Wooldridge (born 1966) is Professor of Computer Science and former Head of the Department of Computer Science at the University of Oxford, Director of Foundational AI Research at the Alan Turing Institute, and Fellow of the AAAI, EurAI, and ACM, having published over 400 scientific papers on multi-agent systems and rational agency.

In [[a-brief-history-of-artificial-intelligence-what-it-is-where-we-are-and-where-we-are-going]] (Flatiron Books / Macmillan, 2020, ISBN 978-1-250-77073-8), Wooldridge chronicles the intellectual history of AI from Alan Turing's 1950 imitation game and the 1956 Dartmouth Workshop through the symbolic 'Golden Age,' the 1973 Lighthill Report AI Winter, expert systems, behavioral robotics, rational agent theory, and the post-2012 deep learning revolution, while rigorously distinguishing narrow statistical mastery from conscious general intelligence (source: BOOKS/AI/a-brief-history-of-artificial-intelligence-what-it-is-where-we-are-and-where-we-are-going.epub, ch. 1–9).

---

mike-amundsen.name: Mike Amundsen
mike-amundsen.eras: 21st-Century Web APIs, Hypermedia Architecture & API Product Strategy
mike-amundsen.bio:
Mike Amundsen is an internationally recognized API architect, speaker, and O'Reilly author who advises enterprises worldwide on RESTful architecture, distributed web design, and API-first digital transformation.

In [[api-strategy-for-decision-makers]] (2022, co-authored with [[derric-gilling]]), Amundsen translates Jobs-to-Be-Done product thinking, non-breaking API evolution, and customer observability into an executive lifecycle strategy (source: BOOKS/Cloud/OReilly-API-Strategy-for-Decision-Makers.pdf, pp. 5–17, 35–47).

---

mikhail-prokopenko.name: Mikhail Prokopenko
mikhail-prokopenko.eras: 21st-Century Complex Systems Science, Information Theory, and Topological Decision Theory
mikhail-prokopenko.bio:
**Mikhail Prokopenko, PhD**, is Professor of Complex Systems in the School of Computer Science and **Director of the Centre for Complex Systems** at the **University of Sydney**, Australia, having previously served as Principal Research Scientist at CSIRO (Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation) (source: [[the-non-orientable-topology-of-condorcets-paradox]], Title Page & References, pp. 1, 18–20). Author of hundreds of peer-reviewed publications and multiple books on guided self-organization, information dynamics, epidemic modeling, and collective intelligence, Prokopenko is internationally recognized for applying information theory, statistical mechanics, and algebraic topology to multi-agent systems and societal decision-making.

In [[the-non-orientable-topology-of-condorcets-paradox]] (2026), co-authored with [[ori-livson]] and [[siddharth-pritam]], Prokopenko investigates the topological foundations of collective rationality. By demonstrating that Condorcet cycles under transitivity induce non-orientable manifolds (the Klein bottle $K$ and real projective plane $\mathbb{RP}^2$) and proving that Arrow's Unrestricted Domain and Non-Dictatorship axioms correspond respectively to orientable and non-orientable social choice spaces (Theorems 6 & 7, pp. 15–16), Prokopenko and his co-authors unify topological social choice with the broader mathematics of self-reference, Gödelian incompleteness, and multi-agent collective intelligence.

---

miroslav-kubat.name: Miroslav Kubat
miroslav-kubat.eras: Late 20th & 21st-Century Inductive Machine Learning, Imbalanced Datasets & Ensemble Classifiers
miroslav-kubat.bio:
Dr. Miroslav Kubat is Associate Professor in the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering at the University of Miami (Coral Gables, Florida), internationally recognized for his pioneering research on learning from imbalanced datasets, decision-tree induction, and radial-basis function networks.

In [[an-introduction-to-machine-learning]] (Springer, Second Edition, 2017, 348 pp., `DOI: 10.1007/978-3-319-63913-0`), Kubat delivers a comprehensive 17-chapter pedagogical synthesis of modern inductive learning—from Bayesian classifiers, Perceptrons, WINNOW, SVMs, and Computational Learning Theory (PAC/VC-dimension) to Bagging, Schapire's Boosting, AdaBoost, Deep Learning, and rigorous statistical performance evaluation (source: BOOKS/AI/2017_Book_AnIntroductionToMachineLearnin.pdf, pp. 1–11, 39–51, 142–151, 245–251).

---

monica-ramona-costache.name: Monica Ramona Costache
monica-ramona-costache.bio:
Monica Ramona Costache is a mathematician trained at the Department of Mathematics, S.N.S. Bucharest, focusing on topological spaces and linear-operator structures underlying quantum theory.

In [[mathematical-foundations-of-quantum-physics]] (2006, with [[adrian-stan]]), she co-authored the Han-sur-Lesse Winterschool primer on Hilbert-space foundations of quantum mechanics (source: BOOKS/Physics/Adrian-Stan-2018 Mathematical Foundations of Quantum Physics.pdf, pp. 1, 3–10).

---

morris-chang.name: Morris Chang
morris-chang.eras: Global Semiconductor Foundry Architecture & East Asian Industrial Strategy
morris-chang.bio:
**Morris Chang** (*Chang Chung-mou*, born 1931) is a Taiwanese-American electrical engineer, industrialist, and founder of **Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC)**—the world's most geopolitically indispensable semiconductor manufacturer. Educated at MIT (B.S. and M.S. in Mechanical Engineering) and Stanford University (Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering), Chang spent twenty-five years at **Texas Instruments**, where he pioneered statistical yield optimization and rose to head TI's global semiconductor business before being recruited in 1985 by Taiwanese technocrat **K. T. Li** to build Taiwan's microchip ecosystem (source: [[chip-war-the-fight-for-the-worlds-most-critical-technology]], Cast of Characters & ch. 29, 37, pp. 7, 166–171, 212–217).

As chronicled by [[chris-miller]] in [[chip-war-the-fight-for-the-worlds-most-critical-technology]], Chang founded **TSMC** in 1987 at age fifty-five around a radical strategic innovation: the **pure-play foundry** that pledged *never* to design its own chips or compete with its customers. By forging TSMC's **"Grand Alliance"** of fabless designers (Apple, Nvidia, Qualcomm, AMD), EDA software firms, and equipment makers (ASML), Chang transformed global computing and positioned Taiwan at the center of 21st-century technological deterrence.

---

mustafa-suleyman.name: Mustafa Suleyman
mustafa-suleyman.eras: 21st-Century Frontier AI Leadership, DeepMind / Microsoft AI & Technological Containment
mustafa-suleyman.bio:
Mustafa Suleyman (CBE) is CEO of Microsoft AI, co-founder and former CEO of Inflection AI, and co-founder and former Head of Applied AI at DeepMind (acquired by Google in 2014).

In [[the-coming-wave-ai-power-and-our-future]] (Crown, 2023, 302 pp., co-authored with [[michael-bhaskar]]; ingested from the 673-entry full-book annotated study notebook `The Coming Wave_ AI, Power, and Our Future - Notebook.html`), Suleyman diagnoses **The Containment Problem** of artificial intelligence and synthetic biology, introduces **Artificial Capable Intelligence (ACI)** and the **Modern Turing Test**, and outlines ten concentric steps to navigate between existential catastrophe and surveillance 'AI-tocracy' (source: BOOKS/AI/The Coming Wave_ AI, Power, and Our Future - Notebook.html, Ch. 1–14, pp. 19–302).

---

naomi-klein.name: Naomi Klein
naomi-klein.eras: 21st-Century Critical Political Economy, Postcolonial Studies & Climate Justice
naomi-klein.bio:
Naomi Klein (born 1970) is a Canadian author, social theorist, and Professor of Climate Justice at the University of British Columbia, known for *No Logo* (1999), *The Shock Doctrine* (2007), *This Changes Everything* (2014), and *Doppelganger: A Trip into the Mirror World* (2023).

In [[doppelganger-israel-palestine-and-the-doppelganger-effect]] (2023), Klein uses the psychoanalytic and literary figure of the **doppelgänger** to analyze how Nazi fascism mirrored European settler-colonial genocides (*'The Nazi in the Mirror'*), how Christian anti-Semitism projected capitalism's abstract domination onto Jews, recovery of the Jewish Labor Bund's principle of ***doikayt* ('hereness')**, and the tragic twin dynamics of Israel and Palestine.

---

neil-rackham.name: Neil Rackham
neil-rackham.eras: Empirical Sales Behavior Analysis & Consultative Enterprise Selling
neil-rackham.bio:
Neil Rackham (born 1936) is a British behavioral psychologist, founder of Huthwaite Inc., and visiting professor at the Universities of Sheffield, Portsmouth, and Cranfield. In the 1970s and 1980s, Rackham led a 30-researcher team that quantitatively coded **35,000 live sales calls** in 23 countries for major global corporations.

In his landmark book [[spin-selling]] (1988), Rackham overturned 60 years of transactional closing dogma, proving that major enterprise sales succeed by converting *Implied Needs* into *Explicit Needs* via **Situation, Problem, Implication, and Need-Payoff (SPIN)** questions.

---

obiora-ike.name: Obiora Ike
obiora-ike.eras: African Social Ethics, Catholic Social Thought, Human Rights & Global Development
obiora-ike.bio:
Monsignor Prof. Dr. Obiora Ike (born 1956) is a Nigerian ethicist, human rights theologian, Founder of the Catholic Institute for Development, Justice and Peace (CIDJAP) in Enugu, Professor of Ethics at Godfrey Okoye University, and Executive Director of Globethics.net in Geneva.

Across [[global-ethics-for-leadership-values-and-virtues-for-life]] (2016) and [[ethics-in-higher-education-values-driven-leaders-for-the-future]] (2017), Ike bridges African communal ethics (*Ubuntu*), the UN 2030 Sustainable Development Goals, and value-driven university teaching.

---

octave-plancherel.name: Octave Plancherel
octave-plancherel.bio:
Octave Plancherel is a cybersecurity researcher at the Cyber-Defence (CYD) Campus of armasuisse Science and Technology in Thun, Switzerland.

Co-editing [[large-language-models-in-cybersecurity-threats-exposure-and-mitigation]] (2024), Plancherel contributes to Switzerland's National Cyberstrategy (NCS) technology monitoring of generative AI threat vectors and mitigation architectures (source: BOOKS/AI/AI LLM Cybesecurity.pdf, pp. 1–6).

---

oliver-schmidt.name: Oliver Schmidt
oliver-schmidt.eras: 21st-Century Clean-Tech Energy Economics, Battery Storage & Experience Curve Modeling
oliver-schmidt.bio:
Dr. Oliver Schmidt is an energy storage economist, Honorary Research Fellow at Imperial College London, and clean-energy industry executive whose research in *Nature Energy* and *Joule* pioneered the application of experience curves and Levelized Cost of Storage (LCOS) across stationary and mobile energy storage.

In [[monetizing-energy-storage-a-toolkit-to-assess-future-cost-and-value]] (2023), co-authored with [[iain-staffell]], Schmidt provides a rigorous techno-economic toolkit for evaluating future costs, revenue stacking, and Long-Duration Energy Storage (LDES) across decarbonizing power grids.

---

ori-livson.name: Ori Livson
ori-livson.eras: 21st-Century Complex Systems, Mathematical Logic, and Topological Social Choice Theory
ori-livson.bio:
**Ori Livson** is a mathematical researcher at the **Centre for Complex Systems** and the **School of Computer Science** at the **University of Sydney**, Australia (source: [[the-non-orientable-topology-of-condorcets-paradox]], Title Page & References, pp. 1, 18–20). Livson's research investigates the deep structural and topological dualities linking mathematical logic, self-referential paradoxes, Kurt Gödel's incompleteness theorems, and collective decision-making in complex systems.

In collaboration with [[siddharth-pritam]] and [[mikhail-prokopenko]] in [[the-non-orientable-topology-of-condorcets-paradox]] (2026), Livson extends Yuliy Baryshnikov's simplicial nerve complex framework of strict preferences to resolve Graciela Chichilnisky's 1980 conjecture on the topological nature of Condorcet's Paradox. By distinguishing valid (intransitive) preference cycles from contradictory (transitive) preference cycles, Livson and his co-authors prove that while valid cycles form orientable surfaces (the cylinder $S^1 \times [0,1]$ and 2-sphere $S^2$), contradictory cycles induce **non-orientable manifolds**—specifically the **Klein bottle** $K$ (when unrealised) and the **real projective plane** $\mathbb{RP}^2$ (when realised)—thereby reformulating Arrow's Impossibility Theorem as a topological incompatibility between orientable and non-orientable social choices.

---

paul-cichonski.name: Paul Cichonski
paul-cichonski.eras: NIST Cybersecurity Standards & Federal Information Security
paul-cichonski.bio:
Paul Cichonski is a computer scientist in the Computer Security Division of the Information Technology Laboratory at the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), where he has led federal standards initiatives on incident response, security automation, and cloud security.

As lead author of [[computer-security-incident-handling-guide-nist-sp-800-61r2]], Cichonski (with [[tom-millar]], [[tim-grance]], and [[karen-scarfone]]) codified the global four-phase incident response lifecycle (*Preparation*, *Detection & Analysis*, *Containment/Eradication/Recovery*, and *Post-Incident Activity*).

---

paul-ducheine.name: Paul Ducheine
paul-ducheine.eras: International Military Law, Cyber Operations Law, Law of Armed Conflict
paul-ducheine.bio:
Brigadier General Prof. Dr. Paul Ducheine is Professor of Cyber Operations and Cyber Security at the Faculty of Military Sciences, Netherlands Defence Academy (NLDA), and Professor of Law of Military Cyber Operations at the Amsterdam Center for International Law, University of Amsterdam. A former combat engineer officer and military legal advisor, Ducheine is a leading European authority on the international legal frameworks governing cyber operations and targeted military coercion.

In *Deterrence in the 21st Century*, Ducheine (with Peter Pijpers) authored Chapter 25 ("The Missing Component in Deterrence Theory: The Legal Framework"), constructing a comprehensive matrix linking deterrence instruments to international legal bases (UN Charter Article 51 self-defence, countermeasures, retorsion, and necessity).

---
paul-ducheine.recurring_themes:
- [[cross-domain-conflict]]: International legal boundaries of grey-zone coercion and countermeasures.
- [[hybrid-threats-and-cyber-warfare]]: Legal basis for state responses to cyber and hybrid operations.

paul-van-hooft.name: Paul van Hooft
paul-van-hooft.eras: Contemporary [[strategic-studies]], Grand Strategy, Transatlantic & Indo-Pacific Security
paul-van-hooft.bio:
Paul van Hooft is a Senior Strategic Analyst at The Hague Centre for Strategic Studies (HCSS) and former post-doctoral fellow at the Security Studies Program (SSP) at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT). He specializes in grand strategy, extended nuclear deterrence, alliance commitments, and maritime security in East Asia and Europe.

In *Deterrence in the 21st Century*, van Hooft authored Chapter 6 ("The US and Extended Deterrence"), analyzing the structural credibility problems inherent in extended nuclear guarantees.

---
paul-van-hooft.recurring_themes:
- [[nuclear-strategy-and-strategic-stability]]: Extended nuclear deterrence dilemmas and security guarantees.
- [[deterrence-and-coercion]]: Credibility, abandonment, and entrapment risks in alliances.

pui-kei-johnston-chu.name: Pui Kei Johnston Chu
pui-kei-johnston-chu.eras: 21st-Century Multi-Tenant SaaS Data Engineering & Cloud Architecture
pui-kei-johnston-chu.bio:
Pui Kei Johnston Chu is a cloud data architect and Snowflake specialist focusing on scalable multi-tenant storage, workload isolation, and data-application security patterns.

Co-authoring [[architecting-data-intensive-saas-applications]] (2021), Chu contributes architectural blueprints for balancing tenant isolation, compute concurrency, and governance in data-intensive SaaS (source: BOOKS/SaaS/OReilly-Report-Architecting-Data-Intensive-SaaS-Applications.pdf, pp. 3–4, 31–42).

---

richard-dawkins.name: Richard Dawkins
richard-dawkins.eras: Neo-Darwinian Evolutionary Biology, Gene-Centric Selection, and Memetics
richard-dawkins.bio:
**Clinton Richard Dawkins** (born 1941) is an eminent British evolutionary biologist, ethologist, Emeritus Fellow of New College, Oxford, and former University of Oxford Professor for Public Understanding of Science (1995–2008). Studying at Oxford under Nobel Prize-winning ethologist Niko Tinbergen, Dawkins achieved worldwide scientific and literary renown with [[the-selfish-gene]] (*The Selfish Gene*, 1976; 2nd ed. 1989; 30th Anniversary ed. 2006) and *The Extended Phenotype* (1982) (source: [[the-selfish-gene]], Intro to 30th Anniversary Ed., pp. vii–xiv).

Synthesizing the mathematical work of [[william-d-hamilton]], George C. Williams, John Maynard Smith, and Robert Trivers, Dawkins established the **gene-centric view of evolution**—distinguishing between potentially immortal digital **replicators** (genes) and transient organismal **vehicles** ("survival machines"). In Chapter 11 of [[the-selfish-gene]], he coined the term **meme** to describe units of cultural transmission evolving via imitation, and in Chapter 12 (*"Nice Guys Finish First"*), he popularized [[robert-axelrod]] and [[william-d-hamilton]]'s [[the-evolution-of-cooperation]], demonstrating why reciprocal cooperation (**TIT FOR TAT**) flourishes in a world of selfish replicators.

---

richard-g-lipsey.name: Richard G. Lipsey
richard-g-lipsey.eras: Structuralist-Evolutionary Economics, General Purpose Technologies & Theory of the Second Best
richard-g-lipsey.bio:
Richard G. Lipsey (born 1928) is Professor Emeritus of Economics at Simon Fraser University, Founding Director of the Economic Growth and Policy Program at the Canadian Institute for Advanced Research (CIAR), and co-originator (with Kelvin Lancaster) of the celebrated *General Theory of Second Best* (1956).

In [[economic-transformations-general-purpose-technologies-and-long-term-economic-growth]] (2005), co-authored with [[kenneth-i-carlaw]] and [[clifford-t-bekar]], Lipsey formulates the **Structuralist-Evolutionary (S-E)** theory of long-term economic growth driven by 24 historical **General Purpose Technologies (GPTs)** from Neolithic agriculture and Sumerian writing to electricity and the electronic computer.

---

richard-j-evans.name: Richard J. Evans
richard-j-evans.eras: Contemporary Classical Historiography & Ancient Political Review
richard-j-evans.bio:
**Richard J. Evans** is a classical historian and professor of ancient history (associated with the University of South Africa and Cardiff University) specializing in Greek and Roman political biography, Hellenistic Syracuse, and classical historiography. In his 1998 review article in *Scholia* (ns Vol. 7, pp. 153–155, preserved in `ARTICLES-REPORTS/Democracy/World’s First Democracies book review_.pdf` and transcribed via `qwen3.8:latest` multimodal Vision OCR), Evans critically evaluates [[eric-w-robinson]]'s [[the-first-democracies-early-popular-government-outside-athens]].

Evans highlights how the simultaneous eighth-to-sixth-century BC Greek colonization movement across the Mediterranean and Black Sea naturally catalyzed participatory *polis* constitutions in cities such as **Argos, Chios, Cyrene, Mantineia, Naxos, and Syracuse**, exposing the inadequacy of ancient cyclical theories of constitutional change (*anakyklosis*) and confirming that pre-classical democracy was widespread outside Attica despite the surviving source bias toward Athenian writers (source: [[the-first-democracies-early-popular-government-outside-athens]], pp. 1–3 [pp. 153–155]).

---

rita-mcgrath.name: Rita McGrath
rita-mcgrath.eras: Contemporary Corporate Strategy, Discovery-Driven Planning, and Transient Advantage
rita-mcgrath.bio:
**Rita Gunther McGrath, PhD**, is a longtime professor of management at **Columbia Business School**, founder of the advisory firm Valize, and one of the world's most cited authorities on strategy and innovation in uncertain environments (source: [[leading-for-tomorrow]], Foreword & Contributors, pp. 11–14, 333). Consistently ranked in the **Top 10 of the Thinkers50** global management awards and winner of the Thinkers50 #1 Strategy Award, McGrath received the Strategic Management Society's CK Prahalad Award for scholarly impact on practice.

She is the author of several landmark strategy texts, including *Discovery-Driven Growth* (with Ian MacMillan), *The End of Competitive Advantage: How to Keep Your Strategy Moving as Fast as Your Business* (2013), and *Seeing Around Corners: How to Spot Inflection Points in Business Before They Happen* (2019). In her Foreword to [[leading-for-tomorrow]] (2026), McGrath argues that the 20th-century industrial leadership playbook—built around optimizing stable competitive advantages and hierarchical control—has reached a structural inflection point, requiring leaders to govern through distributed sensing, permissionless innovation at the edges, and psychological safety.

---

robert-axelrod.name: Robert Axelrod
robert-axelrod.bio:
Robert Axelrod (born 1943) is an American political scientist, game theorist, and Professor Emeritus of Political Science and Public Policy at the Gerald R. Ford School of Public Policy at the University of Michigan. He is renowned internationally for his interdisciplinary research on the evolution of cooperation, conflict resolution, complex adaptive systems, and decision-making in international security.

Axelrod's landmark 1984 book *The Evolution of Cooperation* transformed game theory and social science by providing rigorous empirical and mathematical proof that cooperative behavior can emerge and stabilize among self-interested actors without an overarching sovereign authority. His work bridges political science, evolutionary biology (working closely with William D. Hamilton), economics, psychology, and artificial intelligence. He was awarded a MacArthur "Genius" Fellowship in 1987 and the National Medal of Science in 2014.

---
robert-axelrod.recurring_themes:
- [[cooperation-and-reciprocity]]: Conditional cooperation, TIT FOR TAT, and reciprocal punishment.
- [[shadow-of-the-future]]: The role of ongoing interactions ($w$) in disincentivizing short-term defection.
- [[evolution-of-strategies]]: Ecological modeling of strategy survival, invasion by cooperative clusters, and collective stability.
- [[rationality-and-decision-making]]: Systematic analysis of why egoistic actors often fail to maximize collective payoffs due to envy or excessive complexity.

robert-bauval.name: Robert Bauval
robert-bauval.bio:
Robert Bauval (born 5 March 1948 in Alexandria, Egypt) is an author, lecturer, and former construction engineer of Belgian and British heritage. Living and working across the Middle East and Africa, Bauval developed an intimate understanding of architectural surveying and celestial alignments.

In 1989, Bauval formulated the **Orion Correlation Theory (OCT)**, which established that the spatial layout and relative magnitudes of the three Giza pyramids (Khufu, Khafre, and Menkaure) mirror the three stars of Orion’s Belt (Alnitak, Alnilam, and Mintaka). In collaboration with Adrian Gilbert in *The Orion Mystery* (1994) and Graham Hancock in *Keeper of Genesis* (1996) and *The Master Game* (2011), Bauval argued that the Giza plateau constitutes an astronomical clock locking into the sky of 10,500 BC—the epoch of *Zep Tepi* ("The First Time") when Orion reached its lowest point on the meridian during the 25,920-year precessional cycle.

robert-d-sindelar.name: Robert D. Sindelar
robert-d-sindelar.eras: 21st-Century Pharmaceutical Sciences, Medicinal Chemistry & Biologics Education
robert-d-sindelar.bio:
Robert D. Sindelar, PhD, FCAHS, is Professor of Pharmaceutical Sciences and Medicine at the University of British Columbia and former Dean of Pharmaceutical Sciences and Research Leader at Providence Health Care.

As co-editor of [[pharmaceutical-biotechnology-fundamentals-and-applications]] (4th Ed., 2013), Sindelar bridges molecular cloning, monoclonal antibodies, and translational clinical therapeutics (source: BOOKS/Health Pharma/2013_Book_PharmaceuticalBiotechnology.pdf, pp. 5–9).

---

robert-m-pirsig.name: Robert M. Pirsig
robert-m-pirsig.eras: 20th-Century American Philosophy, Metaphysics of Quality & Philosophical Fiction
robert-m-pirsig.bio:
Robert M. Pirsig (1928–2017) was an American philosopher and writer educated in biochemistry, philosophy (including studies at Banaras Hindu University in India), and journalism at the University of Minnesota and the University of Chicago.

In his 1974 philosophical masterpiece [[zen-and-the-art-of-motorcycle-maintenance]] (and its 1991 sequel *Lila*), Pirsig formulated the **Metaphysics of Quality**, healing the Western schism between **Romantic** (aesthetic/intuitive) and **Classical** (rational/technological) understanding by showing that pre-intellectual **Quality** (Greek *Arete* / Sanskrit *Dharma*) is the primordial source of both subject and object.

---

robert-schoch.name: Robert Schoch
robert-schoch.eras: Geological Dating of Megaliths, Solar Catastrophism, Paleoclimatology
robert-schoch.bio:
Dr. Robert M. Schoch is an American geologist, geophysicist, and associate professor of natural sciences at Boston University. He holds a Ph.D. in geology and geophysics from Yale University.

Schoch gained international prominence in 1991 when, alongside independent Egyptologist John Anthony West, he conducted geological investigations of the Great Sphinx of Giza. Schoch proved that the pronounced undulating erosion patterns on the Sphinx enclosure walls were caused by prolonged, heavy rainfall rather than wind-blown sand weathering. Because the Giza plateau was hyper-arid throughout dynastic Egyptian history (post-3000 BC) and experienced substantial pluvial precipitation only during the transition out of the last Ice Age (c. 10,000–5000 BC), Schoch concluded that the original core carving of the Sphinx dates back at least to the 7th or 6th millennium BC, if not earlier.

robert-skrob.name: Robert Skrob
robert-skrob.eras: 21st-Century Subscription Retention, Membership Economics & Direct-Response Onboarding
robert-skrob.bio:
Robert Skrob is the founder of Membership Services, Inc. and an advisor who has helped scale more than 1,000 membership associations, SaaS platforms, publishers, and subscription-box businesses by optimizing post-join retention and customer lifetime value.

In [[retention-point-membership-and-subscription-growth]] (2018), Skrob introduces the Retention Point, Member Leader mindset, and automated Member On-Ramp built around delivering the fastest win first (source: BOOKS/SaaS/Robert Skrob - Retention Point_ The Single Biggest Secret to Membership and Subscription Growth for Associations, SAAS, Publishers, Digital Access, Subscription Boxes and all Membership and Subscripti.pdf, pp. 4, 10–16, 83–106).

---

roger-penrose.name: Roger Penrose
roger-penrose.eras: Mathematical Physics, General Relativity, Twistor Theory & Philosophy of Consciousness (2020 Nobel Prize in Physics)
roger-penrose.bio:
Sir Roger Penrose (born 1931) is Rouse Ball Professor Emeritus of Mathematics at the University of Oxford and recipient of the **2020 Nobel Prize in Physics** (for proving that black hole singularity formation is a robust prediction of Einstein's General Theory of Relativity). Renowned for Penrose tilings (quasicrystals), spin networks, twistor theory, and cosmic censorship, Penrose has also reshaped the philosophy of mind.

In [[the-emperors-new-mind-concerning-computers-minds-and-the-laws-of-physics]] (1989/1999), Penrose marshals Turing's halting problem, Gödel's incompleteness theorem, the **Weyl Curvature Hypothesis**, and quantum measurement paradoxes to argue that human mathematical insight and consciousness are fundamentally **non-algorithmic**, requiring objective state-vector reduction in a future theory of **Correct Quantum Gravity (CQG)**.

---

romeo-dean.name: Romeo Dean
romeo-dean.eras: 21st-Century Semiconductor Supply Chain & AI Compute Forecasting
romeo-dean.bio:
Romeo Dean is a computer science researcher at Harvard University and the AI Futures Project specializing in AI hardware supply chains, wafer/packaging bottlenecks, and gigawatt datacenter buildouts.

In [[ai-2027]] (2025), Dean models the FLOP scaling trajectories, Nvidia NVL72 GB300 server architectures, and Taiwan Strait geopolitical dependencies underpinning the 2025–2027 intelligence explosion (source: BOOKS/AI/2025 Book_ai-2027.pdf, pp. 1, 4, 11, 46).

---

ronghuai-huang.name: Ronghuai Huang
ronghuai-huang.eras: Smart Learning Environments, AI in Education & Educational Technology
ronghuai-huang.bio:
Ronghuai Huang is Professor and Co-Dean of the Smart Learning Institute at Beijing Normal University, UNESCO Chair on Artificial Intelligence in Education, and Editor-in-Chief of the *Journal of Computers in Education* and Springer's *Lecture Notes in Educational Technology* series.

In [[educational-technology-a-primer-for-the-21st-century]] (2019), co-authored with [[j-michael-spector]] and [[junfeng-yang]], Huang formulates the **SMART** classroom model (*Showing, Manageable, Accessible, Real-time interactive, Testing*) and 5E smart learning ecology.

---

ronnie-mitra.name: Ronnie Mitra
ronnie-mitra.eras: 21st-Century Microservices, API Design & Socio-Technical Software Architecture
ronnie-mitra.bio:
Ronnie Mitra is a software architect, API strategist, and consultant (Mitra Pandey Consulting, Ltd.) specializing in microservices operating models, Domain-Driven Design, and large-scale digital transformation.

In [[microservices-up-and-running]] (2021, co-authored with [[irakli-nadareishvili]]), Mitra introduces the SEED(S) API-first design method, Team Topologies alignment, and GitOps Kubernetes delivery (source: BOOKS/Cloud/Microservices-Up-and-Running_complete.pdf, pp. 4, 31–72).

---

roy-lindelauf.name: Roy Lindelauf
roy-lindelauf.eras: Mathematical Game Theory, Data Science, Algorithmic Defense
roy-lindelauf.bio:
Prof. Dr. Roy Lindelauf is Professor of Data Science and Military Operations at the Netherlands Defence Academy (NLDA) and Associate Professor of Operations Research at Delft University of Technology (TU Delft). He specializes in game-theoretic modeling, network analysis, algorithmic decision systems, and intelligence analytics.

In *Deterrence in the 21st Century*, Lindelauf authored Chapter 22 ("Nuclear Deterrence in the Algorithmic Age: Game Theory Revisited"), examining the mathematical foundations of classical strategic games (Prisoner's Dilemma, Chicken) and their interaction with automated, AI-driven command and control architectures.

---
roy-lindelauf.recurring_themes:
- [[game-theory]]: Formal modeling of nuclear deterrence, pay-off matrices, and Nash equilibria.
- [[rationality-and-decision-making]]: Algorithmic decision loops and strategic automation.
- [[nuclear-strategy-and-strategic-stability]]: Stability and crisis escalation under algorithmic speed.

samer-salam.name: Samer Salam
samer-salam.eras: 21st-Century Internet of Things, Semantic Technologies & Carrier Networking
samer-salam.bio:
Samer Salam is a Principal Engineer at Cisco Systems specializing in system and software architecture for networking products, semantic technologies, machine reasoning, IoT data management, M2M communications, and carrier-grade Layer 2 protocols.

In [[internet-of-things-from-hype-to-reality]] (2019, co-authored with [[ammar-rayes]]), Salam articulates how IoT bends the classic IP protocol hourglass—requiring a 'second thin waist' for application-service normalization and semantic interoperability (source: BOOKS/IoT/2019_Book_InternetOfThingsFromHypeToReal.pdf, pp. 5, 11, 26).

---

samuel-zilincik.name: Samuel Zilincik
samuel-zilincik.eras: Contemporary [[strategic-studies]], Cross-Domain Coercion, Emotions in Strategy
samuel-zilincik.bio:
Dr. Samuel Zilincik is a strategic analyst and researcher at the Netherlands Defence Academy and The Hague Centre for Strategic Studies (HCSS). He specializes in strategic theory, cross-domain deterrence, and the role of human emotions in international security.

In *Deterrence in the 21st Century*, Zilincik co-authored Chapter 8 ("The Essence of Cross-Domain Deterrence" with Tim Sweijs) and Chapter 24 ("Deterrence: A Continuation of Emotional Life with the Admixture of Violent Means" with Isabelle Duyvesteyn), pioneering the integration of emotion science and multi-domain theory into strategic studies.

---
samuel-zilincik.recurring_themes:
- [[cross-domain-conflict]]: Theoretical modeling of Cross-Domain Deterrence (CDD).
- [[rationality-and-decision-making]]: Emotion-centric models of deterrence and crisis escalation.

sandra-ackerman.name: Sandra Ackerman
sandra-ackerman.eras: Decade of the Brain (1990s) Scientific Synthesis & Biomedical Communication
sandra-ackerman.bio:
Sandra J. Ackerman is an American science writer and editor (affiliated with the National Academy of Sciences, the Institute of Medicine, and *American Scientist*) renowned for translating complex neurobiological research into authoritative public and policy syntheses.

In [[discovering-the-brain]] (1992), written for the **Institute of Medicine / National Academy of Sciences** to inaugurate the 1990s *Decade of the Brain*, Ackerman synthesizes neuroanatomy, PET/MRI functional neuroimaging, the neurogenetics of mental illness, synaptic receptor chemistry, and Long-Term Potentiation (LTP).

---

sandro-skansi.name: Sandro Skansi
sandro-skansi.eras: 21st-Century Philosophical Engineering, Logic & Deep Neural Networks
sandro-skansi.bio:
Dr. Sandro Skansi is Associate Professor of Logic and Data Science at the University of Zagreb (Croatia), specializing in the intersection of formal logic, cognitive science, and deep neural networks.

In [[introduction-to-deep-learning-from-logical-calculus-to-artificial-intelligence]] (Springer *Undergraduate Topics in Computer Science*, 2018, 196 pp., `DOI: 10.1007/978-3-319-73004-2`), Skansi defines artificial intelligence as **'philosophical engineering'**—tracing a continuous conceptual arc from McCulloch and Pitts's 1943 logical calculus of neurons and Minsky's XOR critique to modern CNNs, LSTMs, autoencoders, and generative deep learning (source: BOOKS/AI/2018_Book_IntroductionToDeepLearning.pdf, pp. 1–15, 90–101, 142–151).

---

santi-segui.name: Santi Seguí
santi-segui.eras: 21st-Century Data Science, Recommender Systems & Biomedical Machine Learning
santi-segui.bio:
Dr. Santi Seguí is Associate Professor in the Department of Mathematics and Computer Science at the Universitat de Barcelona (Spain), specializing in machine learning, recommender systems, and medical image analytics.

Co-authoring [[introduction-to-data-science-a-python-approach-to-concepts-techniques-and-applications]] (2017) with [[laura-igual]] (with contributions from Jordi Vitrià, Eloi Puertas, Petia Radeva, Oriol Pujol, Sergio Escalera, Francesc Dantí, and Lluís Garrido), Seguí develops reproducible Jupyter Notebook case studies across supervised/unsupervised learning, collaborative filtering, and graph analytics (source: BOOKS/AI/2017_Book_IntroductionToDataScience.pdf, pp. 4–11, 169–181).

---

saturnino-l-salas.name: Saturnino L. Salas
saturnino-l-salas.bio:
Saturnino L. Salas is an American mathematician renowned for his clear, proof-oriented exposition of single- and multivariable calculus, scrutinizing every definition and theorem for conceptual precision.

In [[calculus-one-and-several-variables]] (10th Ed., 2007, with [[einar-hille]] and [[garret-j-etgen]]), Salas anchors calculus on limits, derivatives, integrals, infinite series, and vector calculus (source: BOOKS/Math/C A L C U L U S_ONE AND SEVERAL VARIABLES Artun.pdf, pp. 7–11).

---

scott-alexander.name: Scott Alexander
scott-alexander.bio:
Scott Alexander Siskind is a psychiatrist and author of the influential rationalist publications *Slate Star Codex* and *Astral Codex Ten*.

As co-author of [[ai-2027]] (2025), Alexander synthesizes technical scaling laws, wargaming exercises, and alignment failure modes into a concrete chronological narrative of the 2025–2028 intelligence explosion (source: BOOKS/AI/2025 Book_ai-2027.pdf, pp. 1–36).

---

scott-barry-kaufman.name: Scott Barry Kaufman
scott-barry-kaufman.eras: 21st-Century Humanistic Psychology, Positive Psychology, and Intelligence Research
scott-barry-kaufman.bio:
**Scott Barry Kaufman, PhD**, is a cognitive scientist, humanistic psychologist, and Founder and Director of the **Center for Human Potential** (source: [[leading-for-tomorrow]], About the Editors, p. 339). Earning his PhD in cognitive psychology from **Yale University** and an MPhil in experimental psychology from the **University of Cambridge** under a Gates Cambridge Scholarship, Kaufman has taught at Columbia University, the University of Pennsylvania, and New York University, and hosts *The Psychology Podcast*, which has garnered over 30 million downloads.

Named by *Business Insider* as one of "50 Groundbreaking Scientists Who Are Changing the Way We See the World," Kaufman is the author or editor of more than ten books—including *Ungifted: Intelligence Redefined*, *Wired to Create*, *Transcend: The New Science of Self-Actualization* (which reimagined Abraham Maslow's hierarchy of needs as a dynamic sailboat metaphor), and *Rise Above* (2025). In [[leading-for-tomorrow]] (2026), co-edited with [[chris-shipley]], Kaufman synthesizes contemporary humanistic psychology with executive strategy, arguing that tomorrow's leaders must move from defensive ego-protection ("security needs") toward growth-oriented self-transcendence, psychological safety, and post-traumatic growth.

---

scott-d-lowe.name: Scott D. Lowe
scott-d-lowe.eras: 21st-Century Hyperconverged Infrastructure, Enterprise Cloud & Datacenter Modernization
scott-d-lowe.bio:
Scott D. Lowe is a veteran enterprise IT architect, former CIO, prolific technical author, and cofounder of ActualTech Media specializing in virtualization, flash storage, software-defined datacenters, and hyperconverged infrastructure.

In [[enterprise-cloud-for-dummies-nutanix-special-edition]] (2016), Lowe explains how collapsing compute and storage into hyperconverged Enterprise Clouds unites public-cloud agility with private-cloud control (source: BOOKS/Cloud/Book Enterprise Cloud for Dummies_.pdf, pp. 3–11, 27–40).

---

semra-oguz.name: Semra Oğuz
semra-oguz.bio:
Specialist Physiotherapist Semra Oğuz focuses on neurological rehabilitation and daily-mobility exercise protocols for patients living with Parkinson's disease and movement disorders.

In [[parkinson-hastaligi-hasta-ve-yakinlari-icin-el-kitabi]] (2013), she co-authored the structured physical-therapy and posture/gait training programs empowering patient independence (source: BOOKS/Health Pharma/Parkinson-Hastaligi-Hasta-ve-Yakinlari-icin-El-Kitabi.pdf, pp. 1, 6).

---

shoshana-maraney.name: Shoshana Maraney
shoshana-maraney.eras: 21st-Century Ecommerce Fraud Analytics, Identity Trust & Financial Crime Defense
shoshana-maraney.bio:
Shoshana Maraney is a Cambridge University–educated fraud-prevention specialist and industry analyst with extensive experience in ecommerce and fintech identity verification at Forter and Identiq.

Co-authoring [[practical-fraud-prevention]] (2022) with [[gilit-saporta]], Maraney bridges fraud research, customer-experience preservation, and cross-departmental defense against stolen cards, mules, friendly fraud, and money laundering (source: BOOKS/Cloud/3683-practical-fraud-prevention.pdf, pp. 2, 19–214).

---

sibel-ozekmekci.name: Sibel Özekmekçi
sibel-ozekmekci.eras: 21st-Century Clinical Neurology, Parkinson's Disease & Movement Disorders (Türkiye)
sibel-ozekmekci.bio:
Prof. Dr. Sibel Özekmekçi is an emeritus professor of neurology from Istanbul University Cerrahpaşa Faculty of Medicine's Parkinson's Disease and Movement Disorders Unit and a pioneer of Parkinson's patient advocacy and education in Türkiye.

In [[parkinson-hastaligi-hasta-ve-yakinlari-icin-el-kitabi]] (5th Ed., 2013, with [[hulya-apaydin]], [[semra-oguz]], and [[ismail-zileli]]), she demystifies dopaminergic therapy and multidisciplinary care (source: BOOKS/Health Pharma/Parkinson-Hastaligi-Hasta-ve-Yakinlari-icin-El-Kitabi.pdf, pp. 1–5, 10).

---

siddharth-pritam.name: Siddharth Pritam
siddharth-pritam.eras: 21st-Century Computational Topology, Applied Algebraic Topology, and Combinatorial Geometry
siddharth-pritam.bio:
**Siddharth Pritam** is a mathematician and faculty member in the Department of Computer Science at the **Chennai Mathematical Institute (CMI)**, India (source: [[the-non-orientable-topology-of-condorcets-paradox]], Title Page, p. 1). Formerly a postdoctoral researcher at INRIA (DataShape) in France and the Institute of Science and Technology Austria (ISTA), Pritam specializes in computational topology, topological data analysis (TDA), persistent homology, simplicial collapse, and nerve complexes of posets.

In [[the-non-orientable-topology-of-condorcets-paradox]] (2026), co-authored with [[ori-livson]] and [[mikhail-prokopenko]], Pritam brings combinatorial and algebraic topology to social choice theory—constructing explicit triangulations of preference nerves $\mathcal{N}(\mathcal{U})$ and $\mathcal{N}(\mathcal{V})$ and proving via 2-sheeted covering maps and Euler characteristic calculations ($\chi(\mathbb{RP}^2) = \frac{1}{2}\chi(S^2) = 1$) that realising a contradictory Condorcet cycle transforms the preference sphere into the non-orientable real projective plane $\mathbb{RP}^2$ (Theorem 5 & Appendix A.1, Theorem A.2, pp. 11–13, 21–23).

---

stat-news-editorial.name: STAT News Editorial Team
stat-news-editorial.eras: 21st-Century Investigative Biomedical Journalism, Biotechnology & Regulatory Reporting
stat-news-editorial.bio:
STAT News (founded in Boston in 2015) is a premier health, medicine, and life-sciences journalism organization covering biomedical breakthroughs, biotech boardrooms, clinical trials, and FDA policy.

In [[beyond-cancer-the-expanding-reach-of-cell-and-gene-therapies]] (September 2026), STAT journalists (including Isabella Cueto, Megan Molteni, Paul Knoepfler, Jason Mast, and Allison DeAngelis) chronicle CAR-T's leap into autoimmunity, in-utero and bespoke CRISPR gene editing, FDA oversight shifts, and single-shot in-vivo CAR-T engineering (source: BOOKS/Health Pharma/2026 STAT_Ebook_BeyondCancer_September2026.pdf, pp. 2–5, 7–69).

---

stefan-soesanto.name: Stefan Soesanto
stefan-soesanto.eras: Cyber Warfare, Defense Technology, Information Security
stefan-soesanto.bio:
Stefan Soesanto is Senior Cyber Defense Researcher in the Risk and Resilience Team at the Center for Security Studies (CSS) at ETH Zurich. He specializes in state-sponsored cyber operations, cyber defense posture, and intelligence warfare.

In *Deterrence in the 21st Century*, Soesanto (with Max Smeets) authored Chapter 20 ("Cyber Deterrence: The Past, Present, and Future"), deconstructing the structural obstacles to effective cyber deterrence.

---
stefan-soesanto.recurring_themes:
- [[hybrid-threats-and-cyber-warfare]]: Cyber operations, attribution dilemmas, and exploit perishability.
- [[cross-domain-conflict]]: Cross-domain responses to offensive cyber operations.

stefanie-von-hlatky.name: Stéfanie von Hlatky
stefanie-von-hlatky.eras: 21st-Century Transatlantic Security Studies, NATO Interoperability & Defense Policy
stefanie-von-hlatky.bio:
**Stéfanie von Hlatky** is Professor of Political Studies, Canada Research Chair in Gender, Security, and the Armed Forces, and former Director of the **Centre for International and Defence Policy (CIDP)** at **Queen's University** in Kingston, Ontario. An authority on alliance deterrence, NATO burden-sharing, military interoperability, and the human dimension of warfare, she co-edited [[developing-the-super-soldier-enhancing-military-performance]] (*Developing the Super Soldier: Enhancing Military Performance*, 2017, with [[william-g-braun-iii]] and [[kim-richard-nossal]]) (source: [[developing-the-super-soldier-enhancing-military-performance]], pp. 1–6, viii).

Her scholarship bridges transatlantic alliance politics (aligning with [[sten-rynning]] and [[paul-van-hooft]] in [[deterrence-in-the-21st-century]]) with the operational, ethical, and unit-cohesion implications of emerging military technologies and human performance enhancement.

---

sten-rynning.name: Sten Rynning
sten-rynning.bio:
Sten Rynning is Professor of Political Science and Vice-Dean for Research at the University of Southern Denmark (SDU), where he founded the Center for War Studies. He is a leading European scholar on NATO strategy, modern warfare, and European defense cooperation.

In *Deterrence in the 21st Century*, Rynning authored Chapter 3 ("Deterrence Rediscovered: NATO and Russia"), examining the alliance's pivot back to collective defense and the complex relationship between deterrence and political dialogue.

---
sten-rynning.recurring_themes:
- [[deterrence-and-coercion]]: NATO collective territorial defense and forward posture against Russian revanchism.
- [[strategic-studies]]: Alliance dynamics and transatlantic security architecture.

stephan-fackler.name: Stephan Fackler
stephan-fackler.eras: 21st-Century Functional Analysis, Operator Theory & Mathematical Physics
stephan-fackler.bio:
Stephan Fackler is a German mathematician at Ulm University specializing in functional analysis, operator semigroups, spectral theory, and harmonic analysis.

In [[mathematical-foundations-of-quantum-mechanics-ulm-lecture-notes]] (2015), Fackler constructs measure theory, unbounded self-adjoint operators, the Spectral Theorem, Stone's Theorem, Kato–Rellich perturbation theory, and tempered distributions for graduate physicists and mathematicians (source: BOOKS/Physics/Ulm notes_mathematical_found_Quantum Mechanics.pdf, pp. 1–7).

---

stephen-hawking.name: Stephen Hawking
stephen-hawking.eras: 20th/21st-Century Theoretical Cosmology, Black-Hole Thermodynamics & Quantum Gravity
stephen-hawking.bio:
Professor Stephen W. Hawking, CH, CBE, FRS (1942–2018) was the Lucasian Professor of Mathematics at the University of Cambridge (1979–2009) and one of the preeminent theoretical physicists of the modern era, celebrated for the Penrose–Hawking singularity theorems, the discovery of thermal Hawking radiation from black holes, the Hartle–Hawking No-Boundary cosmological proposal, and global science communication.

Across four landmark works in this wiki—[[a-brief-history-of-time]] (1988), [[the-theory-of-everything-origin-and-fate-of-the-universe]] (2005), [[the-grand-design]] (2010, with [[leonard-mlodinow]]), and [[brief-answers-to-the-big-questions]] (2018)—Hawking bridges spacetime singularity physics, M-theory, model-dependent realism, space colonization, and existential AI risk (source: BOOKS/Physics/A Brief History of Time ( PDFDrive ).pdf, pp. 4–7; BOOKS/Physics/Brief Answers to the Big Questions ( PDFDrive ).pdf, pp. 5–18).

---

stephen-stockwell.name: Stephen Stockwell
stephen-stockwell.eras: 21st-Century Comparative Democratic History, Classical Rhetoric & Media Studies
stephen-stockwell.bio:
**Stephen Stockwell** is Professor Emeritus of Journalism and Communication at Griffith University, Australia, and a scholar of political communication, rhetoric, and the global history of democratic institutions. Co-editor (with [[benjamin-isakhan]]) of [[the-secret-history-of-democracy-primitive-democracy]] (*The Secret History of Democracy*, 2011), Stockwell authored the volume's Introduction (*"Democracy and History"*), Chapter 2 (*"Before Athens: Early Popular Government in Phoenicia and Greek City-States"*, pp. 35–48), Chapter 7 (*"Democratic Culture in the Early Venetian Republic"*, pp. 105–120), and the Conclusion (*"Democratizing the History of Democracy"*, pp. 219–224).

Stockwell's research demonstrates how maritime trading networks across Levantine Phoenician city-states (Byblos, Sidon, Tyre, and their western colony Carthage) and early archaic Greek poleis developed powerful citizen assemblies (*'am*) and suffete magistracies that directly mediated the transmission of participatory governance from the Bronze Age Near East into the Mediterranean basin—complementing [[eric-w-robinson]]'s findings in [[the-first-democracies-early-popular-government-outside-athens]].

---

susan-mcclary.name: Susan McClary
susan-mcclary.eras: New Musicology, Feminist Music Criticism & Cultural History
susan-mcclary.bio:
Susan McClary (born 1946) is a MacArthur Fellow and Professor of Musicology (affiliated with UCLA, McGill, and Case Western Reserve University) who co-founded the 'New Musicology' (*Feminine Endings*, 1991), dismantling formalist claims that Western classical and popular music are autonomous, purely mathematical structures detached from gender, power, and ideology.

In her Afterword (*'The Politics of Silence and Sound'*) to [[jacques-attali]]'s [[noise-the-political-economy-of-music]], McClary connects Attali's fourth network (*Composing*) to avant-garde classical music, punk, New Wave, and vernacular musical resistance.

---

the-giving-block.name: The Giving Block
the-giving-block.eras: 21st-Century Crypto Philanthropy, Web3 Fundraising & Nonprofit Innovation
the-giving-block.bio:
The Giving Block is a cryptocurrency and NFT fundraising infrastructure platform enabling charities, hospitals, universities, and social-impact foundations to accept and process digital-asset philanthropy.

In [[crypto-and-nft-philanthropy-afsp-case-study]] (2022), The Giving Block documents how the American Foundation for Suicide Prevention raised $400,000 in crypto and NFT donations during 2021 (source: BOOKS/Anthropology_/CASE STUDY-TGB-AFSP.pdf, p. 1).

---

thomas-larsen.name: Thomas Larsen
thomas-larsen.eras: 21st-Century AI Alignment Research & Quantitative AGI Forecasting
thomas-larsen.bio:
Thomas Larsen is an AI alignment researcher and co-founder of the Center for AI Policy and the AI Futures Project, specializing in mechanistic interpretability, deceptive alignment, and recursive R&D multipliers.

In [[ai-2027]] (2025), Larsen models the technical progression from `Agent-1` coding automation to adversarial misalignment in `Agent-4` and `Agent-5` (source: BOOKS/AI/2025 Book_ai-2027.pdf, pp. 1, 6–36, 51–61).

---

thomas-sowell.name: Thomas Sowell
thomas-sowell.eras: Chicago School Economics, Intellectual History & Comparative Social Philosophy
thomas-sowell.bio:
Thomas Sowell (born 1930) is the Rose and Milton Friedman Senior Fellow on Public Policy at the Hoover Institution, Stanford University. Educated at Harvard, Columbia, and the University of Chicago (under George Stigler and Milton Friedman), Sowell is the author of over forty books on economics, intellectual history, knowledge and decisions, and ethnic studies.

In his personal favorite among his own works, [[a-conflict-of-visions-ideological-origins-of-political-struggles]] (1987/2007), Sowell traces two centuries of political, legal, and economic battles to the foundational clash between the **Constrained (Tragic) Vision** (Smith, Burke, Hamilton, Hayek—relying on systemic incentives and trade-offs) and the **Unconstrained (Utopian) Vision** (Godwin, Condorcet, Rousseau, Dworkin—relying on articulated elite reason and solutions).

---

thorkild-jacobsen.name: Thorkild Jacobsen
thorkild-jacobsen.eras: 20th-Century Assyriology, Sumerology & Ancient Near Eastern Institutional History
thorkild-jacobsen.bio:
**Thorkild Peter Rudolph Jacobsen** (1904–1993) was a Danish-born American historian, philologist, and one of the twentieth century's foremost Assyriologists and scholars of Sumerian literature, serving as Director of the Oriental Institute at the University of Chicago and later Professor of Assyriology at Harvard University. In his groundbreaking July 1943 article *"Primitive Democracy in Ancient Mesopotamia"* (*Journal of Near Eastern Studies* 3/2, pp. 159–172)—examined directly in `ARTICLES-REPORTS/Democracy/HW2-1--Democracy-in-Mesopotamia.pdf` and expanded in [[the-secret-history-of-democracy-primitive-democracy]]—Jacobsen overturned the prevailing view that ancient Mesopotamia knew only theocratic autocracy.

Through close reading of Sumerian and Akkadian cuneiform texts, including *Gilgamesh and Agga*, the *Epic of Gilgamesh*, *Enuma Elish*, and Old Assyrian merchant archives from Kanesh (Kültepe in Anatolia), Jacobsen demonstrated that third-millennium BC Mesopotamian city-states were governed by a bicameral general assembly (*ukkin* / *puhrum*) of elders (*abba*) and free arms-bearing citizens (*guruš*).
